text:
The Catholic Church celebrates today the birth of the Blessed Virgin Mary on its traditional fixed date of September 8, nine months after the December 8 celebration of her Immaculate Conception as the child of Saints Joachim and Anne.

The circumstances of the Virgin Mary's infancy and early life are not directly recorded in the Bible, but other documents and traditions describing the circumstances of her birth are cited by some of the earliest Christian writers from the first centuries of the Church.

These accounts, although not considered authoritative in the same manner as the Bible, outline some of the Church's traditional beliefs about the birth of Mary.

The “Protoevangelium of James,” which was probably put into its final written form in the early second century, describes Mary's father Joachim as a wealthy member of one of the Twelve Tribes of Israel. Joachim was deeply grieved, along with his wife Anne, by their childlessness. “He called to mind Abraham,” the early Christian writing says, “that in the last day God gave him a son Isaac.”

Joachim and Anne began to devote themselves extensively and rigorously to prayer and fasting, initially wondering whether their inability to conceive a child might signify God's displeasure with them.

As it turned out, however, the couple were to be blessed even more abundantly than Abraham and Sarah, as an angel revealed to Anne when he appeared to her and prophesied that all generations would honor their future child: “The Lord has heard your prayer, and you shall conceive, and shall bring forth, and your seed shall be spoken of in all the world.”

After Mary's birth, according to the Protoevangelium of James, Anne “made a sanctuary” in the infant girl's room, and “allowed nothing common or unclean” on account of the special holiness of the child. The same writing records that when she was one year old, her father “made a great feast, and invited the priests, and the scribes, and the elders, and all the people of Israel.”

“And Joachim brought the child to the priests,” the account continues, “and they blessed her, saying: 'O God of our fathers, bless this child, and give her an everlasting name to be named in all generations' . . . And he brought her to the chief priests, and they blessed her, saying: 'O God most high, look upon this child, and bless her with the utmost blessing, which shall be for ever.'”

The protoevangelium goes on to describe how Mary's parents, along with the temple priests, subsequently decided that she would be offered to God as a consecrated Virgin for the rest of her life, and enter a chaste marriage with the carpenter Joseph.

Saint Augustine described the birth of the Blessed Virgin Mary as an event of cosmic and historic significance, and an appropriate prelude to the birth of Jesus Christ. “She is the flower of the field from whom bloomed the precious lily of the valley,” he said.

The fourth-century bishop, whose theology profoundly shaped the Western Church's understanding of sin and human nature, affirmed that “through her birth, the nature inherited from our first parents is changed."

The traditional Onam Sadya service at Sabarimala was limited during this year’s Onam festival, which has really disappointed the devotees of Swami Ayyappa. It has been a 70-year-old tradition of serving/offering Sadya to Ayyappa devotees during the temple opening days of Onam.

The TDB President, Mr. K. Jayakumar, IAS, has been bringing many reforms to the Sabarimala administrative system, as it appears from his interviews. In his interviews, he said that traditional Kerala Sadya would be offered to Ayyappa devotees during the Mandalakalam. This was very much appreciated, but it has not materialised to the extent or in the manner in which the matter was promoted.

The TDB President has stated that his office is refusing to accept sponsorships from unauthorised persons and has also mentioned that there are many power brokers operating at Sabarimala. The TDB office has also stated that, during this Onam period, it did not accept private sponsorships as part of the reforms.

Is #Sabarimala being run or managed only with the financial assistance or sponsorship of unauthorised or high-profile people?

Is Sabarimala not managed through the kanikka or contributions of ordinary and poor Ayyappa devotees?

The #TDBPresident has stated that Onam Sadya was served to 3,000 devotees, and I kindly request that the feedback of ordinary and poor devotees also be heard and given due attention. It appears that the staff may not be conveying the actual situation and feedback to the #TDB office.

The TDB President has stated that the sponsorship reforms have affected the brokers and beneficiaries, and that they are the ones creating confusion and spreading rumours. Sir, if you knew very well that such a situation could arise, why did your office allow or give space for such confusion and rumours? Why did the office not act wisely and proactively to prevent such a situation? You have repeatedly stated in your interviews that there are many brokers involved in Sabarimala sponsorships and that they are benefiting from the system.

The 70-year-old traditional #Onam #Sadya service during the temple opening days was not available in its usual form this time. Onam Sadya was served only to a limited number of #Ayyappa devotees, while priority was reportedly given to Kerala Government staff. The TDB President said in his interview that items such as pulao would be removed from the menu and that Sadya would be offered to all devotees visiting during the Mandalakalam. However, Ayyappa devotees do not want a completely new Sadya service from the TDB; they want the old and traditional Onam Sadya service to continue. Previously, it was usually served for three days under individual sponsorships.

It is unfortunate that the TDB and the Government are saying that the delay in fund allocation, confusion and changes to the Onam Sadya service—which has been a 70-year-old tradition at Sabarimala—are due to the reforms in the sponsorship system.

The TDB President has been mentioning sponsorship reforms since the beginning of his tenure. Therefore, the TDB office should have prepared and planned well in advance to ensure that this traditional Onam Sadya service continued without any confusion or interruption. It is the prime duty of the TDB to preserve and continue the traditional practices of Sabarimala.

It is unfortunate to say that the sufferings of Ayyappa devotees continue, and there is genuine concern when thinking about the upcoming Mandala and Makaravilakku seasons, particularly the difficulties that ordinary and poor devotees may face.

Reforms are welcome, but they should not come at the cost of long-standing traditions or the convenience of ordinary devotees.

   — By an Ayyappa devotee, not by someone influenced by sponsors.

During the grand Kalmeshwara Rathotsava festival held in Mudhol, Bagalkot district, local police personnel drew immense praise from the public for offering special prayers and respects to the holy chariot. As the sacred chariot passed right in front of the Mudhol police station, police officers and staff gathered together to offer traditional pooja and seek blessings.  Managing tight security and law and order duties during the massive procession, the police officers demonstrated a people-friendly approach through their respectful act. text:
The World Gets a Vote. It Does Not Get a Veto.

I hear a lot of noise from outside about what will happen to us if we do this, or dare to do that. Sanctions. Isolation. Consequences. It always arrives in the same tone, the one reserved for people who are expected to be grateful for the warning.

Here is a thought. Stop asking.

Israel should make all of Israel actually be Israel. Judea and Samaria. Gaza. Not as a provocation, and not because a headline made someone angry, but because a nation that holds its sovereignty conditional on foreign approval does not have sovereignty. It has a permit. Permits get revoked.

The people warning us have leverage in exactly one place: our willingness to believe them.

Look at what the world does, as opposed to what it says. It buys from us. Israeli defense exports are at record levels, and the buyers include governments whose foreign ministries condemn us in the morning and sign procurement contracts in the afternoon. Air defense. Radar. Drones. Electronic warfare. The same capitals lecturing us on restraint want our interceptors over their own cities.

It goes well past weapons. Israel reclaims close to ninety percent of its wastewater, the highest rate on earth, and the country in second place is under thirty. Most of what comes out of an Israeli tap started in the Mediterranean. Drip irrigation was invented here and now feeds farmland on six continents. Capsule endoscopy, so a patient swallows a camera instead of being cut open, was developed here. Teva puts generic medicine in more cabinets than any company alive. After the United States, more cybersecurity capital flows into this country than anywhere on the planet.

That is not a boast. It is a description of dependency, and it runs one direction.

Now the part people who have not looked it up will get wrong.

The measures were real. They were tried. Here is what happened.

In August 2025, after the cabinet decision on Gaza City, Germany suspended approval of military exports that could be used there. Spain declared a full embargo. Italy, Canada, the Netherlands and Belgium imposed limits. Britain suspended dozens of licences while insisting the word embargo did not apply.

On the 24th of November, twelve weeks later, Germany reversed and went back to case-by-case review. Our foreign minister publicly invited the rest of them to follow.

And in the year those measures were in force, Israeli defense exports reached 19.2 billion dollars. Up almost thirty percent on the year before. The fifth consecutive record. More than half of it government to government, roughly ten billion dollars signed by states directly, which means signed by cabinets, which means signed by the same people who wrote the statements.

Did Europe cut? Yes. European purchasing fell from fifty four percent of our exports to thirty six, about a billion dollars in real money. That is not nothing and I will not pretend it is.

It also did not matter. Asia Pacific nearly doubled, from 3.4 billion to 6.1. The Gulf rose. We now sell more to our Arab neighbours than to the United States. And the single largest category we export, twenty nine percent of everything, is air defense and missiles. The precise thing they announce they will stop buying is the precise thing they keep buying.

They ran the experiment. We closed the year with a record.

"It Was Never Yours"

Someone will say the land was never ours to claim. Answer it directly, because the answer is documented.

Start with the name. "West Bank" is a Jordanian invention from 1950, coined when Jordan annexed the territory and needed a way to distinguish it from the east bank of the river. Before that nobody on earth called it that. On every map for the previous two thousand years it is Judea and Samaria.

Then the chain of title.

San Remo, April 1920. The Allied Powers assign the Mandate for Palestine with the Jewish national home written into it. The League of Nations confirms it in 1922, and Article 6 obliges the Mandatory to facilitate Jewish immigration and close settlement on the land.

That same year, Britain uses Article 25 to sever everything east of the Jordan River, roughly seventy seven percent of the territory, and close it to Jewish settlement. That becomes Transjordan, and then Jordan. Understand what that means. An Arab state was carved out of Mandate Palestine in 1922. The partition everybody keeps demanding already happened, a century ago, and it took three quarters of the map.

Article 80 of the UN Charter preserved those Mandate rights. They did not evaporate in 1948.

In 1947 a second partition was offered. The Arab Higher Committee and the Arab League rejected it and went to war. That is why no Arab state emerged in 1948. Not because anyone was expelled from the negotiating table, but because the leadership of the day preferred the whole thing or nothing and gambled on the war.

They lost the gamble, and Jordan took Judea and Samaria and held it for nineteen years. That annexation was recognized by almost no government on earth. Jordan handed out Jordanian citizenship to the people living there, which is worth remembering every time someone insists those people never had anywhere else to be. Then in July 1988 Jordan renounced every claim to the territory and walked away.

So ask the question plainly. Who holds sovereign title? Not Jordan, which surrendered it. Not a state that was refused in 1947 and never came into being. The last valid international instrument to allocate this land allocated it to us, and nothing since has lawfully taken it back.

Peace First. That Is Also Torah.

I want to live in peace. I mean it plainly, and the Torah means it before it means anything else. Deuteronomy is explicit: when you approach a city to wage war against it, you first call out to it for peace. First. That is not a footnote. It is the opening move, and it is commanded.

But the same Torah refuses to make a virtue of dying politely. The Gemara in Sanhedrin puts it in six words: if someone comes to kill you, rise and kill him first. Learn what that actually is before you quote it at me or at anyone else. It is a law of self defense against a man already coming through your wall. It is bounded on purpose. It is not a licence, and anyone who stretches it into one is not reading Torah, they are decorating a mood with it.

Both are ours. The call for peace first, and the refusal to be slaughtered while the offer is considered. A people holding only the first gets buried. A people holding only the second becomes something it should not want to be. The last hundred years settled the question of what happens to Jews who carry only the first.

October 27

We vote in seven weeks, and the promises have already started.

Every one of them will be delivered with total conviction. Sovereignty. Security. Never again, this time we mean it. Some of them will be wrapped in a verse for effect, and that is the part I want to speak to directly.

If you invoke Torah to win a seat, you have raised the standard on yourself, not lowered it. Numbers is not ambiguous: he shall not profane his word, he shall do everything that proceeds out of his mouth. Deuteronomy goes further and says it is better never to vow at all than to vow and fail to pay. A campaign promise dressed in a pasuk and then quietly dropped in December is not an ordinary broken pledge. It is a chillul Hashem, and it is done in our name.

The Torah has a standard for leadership and it is not charisma. A king writes his own Sefer Torah, keeps it with him, and reads from it all the days of his life, specifically so that his heart is not lifted above his brothers. Not so he can quote it at a rally. So it can rule him.

I am not telling anyone how to vote. I am telling you the measurement. Not what they say in October. What they do in February, when the cameras have moved on and keeping the promise costs something.

Ask them now, on the record, and remember the answer.

We Are Not Going Anywhere

Plenty of people will read this, reach for their phones, and explain why Jews will lose, why Jews will be stopped, why this time the arithmetic finally catches up with us. That argument has a long record. It is undefeated in volume and it has never once been right.

Keep typing.

The words Papa, Pope, and Father share the same basic meaning: "dad" or "spiritual guide". They all started as simple baby talk.

Papa and Pope: Both words trace back to the Greek word pappas, which means "father". It is a "reduplicated" word, meaning it repeats a simple sound a baby makes (like "ba-ba" or "pa-pa"). In early Christianity, this cute, loving title was used for any priest or bishop. Over time, Western Christians started using the Latin version, papa, only for the Bishop of Rome. This eventually turned into the English word #pope.
Father: This word has older roots. It comes from ancient Germanic and Proto-Indo-European languages (like the Old English fæder). It originally sounded like the Latin word pater. Like "pope," it comes from early, natural human babbling sounds for a parent.

text:
The voice behind those steady, heartbreaking words belonged to Brian David Sweeney, a 38-year-old former U.S. Navy pilot, defense contractor, and devoted husband from Spencer, Massachusetts. On the morning of September 11, 2001, he boarded United Airlines Flight 175 out of Boston, bound for Los Angeles.

Brian was a man who lived with an effortless, calm warmth. A charismatic athlete and born leader, he had spent years flying jets for the military before transitioning into defense consulting. He loved the outdoors, loved his family fiercely, and was deeply in love with his wife, Julie, a high school teacher.

When hijackers stormed the cockpit of Flight 175 shortly after takeoff, forcing the plane into a sharp turn toward New York City, Brian didn't panic. Drawing on his military training and instincts, he made his way toward an Airfone on the back of a seatback.
At 8:59 a.m., he dialed home. Julie was at work, teaching her class, so the call went to their answering machine.

With quiet composure, knowing the nightmare unfolding around him, Brian didn't fill his final words with fear or anger. Instead, he stripped life down to its absolute essence: love, permission to be happy, and peace. He left that brief, three-sentence message, a testament to selfless devotion, before placing a second call to his mother, Louise, telling her that the passengers were considering storming the cockpit to retake the plane.

Minutes later, at 9:03 a.m., Flight 175 struck the South Tower of the World Trade Center.

In the years since, Julie Sweeney Roth shared Brian’s voicemail with the National September 11 Memorial & Museum. What could have been a private tragedy became a beacon of grace under fire. His message stands as one of the most poignant artifacts of that day, a reminder that when faced with ultimate darkness, the final impulse of the human spirit is pure, unshakeable love.

In Brian’s final journey his military background kicked in during the crisis, leading him to help organize an active plan to fight back. Seated near the front in the first row of coach when Flight 175 took off, Brian did not remain passive when the hijackers seized control. Instead, he quietly made his way to the back of the aircraft to assess the situation and access a seat-back Airfone. Immediately after leaving the serene, loving voicemail for his wife Julie at 8:59 A.M., he placed a second call to his mother, Louise, revealing the fierce resolve behind his calm words.

During that final call with his mother, Brian confirmed that he and several fellow passengers were actively coordinating in the rear of the cabin, preparing to storm the cockpit and retake control of the airliner. While the heroic passenger revolt on Flight 93 is widely recognized, Brian's final words to his mother offer rare proof that the passengers on Flight 175 were also mounting a courageous resistance in their final moments on board.

text:
India just cleared ₹1.1 lakh cr of defence buys. AoN accorded. 98% Indian industry. Good headline.

The Navy headline that actually matters is the indigenous Marine Gas Turbines. This could be HUGE or it could be a damp squib depending on where it goes from here on. 

“Design, development and subsequent procurement” must *mean* all three words.
Design: Indian reference design, Indian IP, Indian test data. Not a licensed drawing with a new nameplate.
Development: hot-section metallurgy, controls, marinisation, shock, salt, endurance. The ugly slog years. Not a nice looking brochure.
Procurement: a production order large enough that a company will actually tool up. One prototype does not create an industry. A class of ships does.

If any of those three is missing, we will be back to import substitution theatre.

If this becomes a real engine programme, it is Atmanirbharta. If it becomes a committee + imported core + a “Make in India” sticker, we would have just lost an opportunity. 

Propulsion is the last big choke-point. Every delay in an indigenous MGT is not an engineering delay. It is a sovereignty delay that shows up ten years later as a possible constraint. That is why it may be better to even accept the delay rather than compromise on the end aim. Tough choice. 

Though I am sure, the @indiannavy has things well worked out, IMHO Marine gas turbines will need a programme, not a captive project: private yards that will fit them, MSMEs that will make blades, casings, controls & test rigs and a Navy that is allowed to be an impatient customer instead of a polite committee member.

The moment (and *if*) the only ‘industry partner’ turns out to be  from amongst the ‘usual suspects’, the cow path has already been surveyed for being paved. Atmanirbharta in propulsion will be real only when more than one Indian factory can be pushed….and pushed hard. 

My one question to *serving* officers (not to veterans like me on panels and not even those serving in the technical directorates) for them to ponder on….
When the first indigenous MGT is offered to a ship class, will you accept a slightly lower “brochure” number in exchange for control over the spares, the upgrades and the next hull? Or will the staff requirement still be written so that only the foreign engines can “meet it”?

That single choice will decide whether yesterday’s DAC note was transformational or just better asphalt on the same trail.

(PS: For the trail -asphalt analogy see my post a few days ago about ‘paving a cow path’).

text:
The Crown's Promise, Not the Colonies': Emancipation and the American Revolution

During the American Revolution, the promise of freedom in exchange for military service against Great Britain did not come from the thirteen colonies or their revolutionary governments — it came from the British Crown. A popular but historically inaccurate narrative holds that the rebelling colonies, particularly in the South, offered enslaved African Americans their freedom if they took up arms against the British. The historical record shows the opposite: it was British officials, beginning with Lord Dunmore's Proclamation of 1775 and expanded by the Philipsburg Proclamation of 1779, who offered emancipation to enslaved people who fled their patriot masters and joined the royal cause. When southern patriots did entertain the idea of freeing enslaved men for military service, as in John Laurens's proposal to the Continental Congress, their own state legislatures rejected it outright. The southern colonies-turned-states did not grant freedom to slaves for Revolutionary War service; the practice and the policy belonged to Britain.

The clearest evidence of British initiative is Lord Dunmore's Proclamation, issued on November 7, 1775, by John Murray, the royal governor of Virginia. Dunmore declared martial law and promised freedom to "all indented servants, negroes, or others" belonging to rebel masters who were willing and able to bear arms for the Crown. Between eight hundred and two thousand enslaved men answered the call, forming what became known as Lord Dunmore's Ethiopian Regiment, whose members reportedly wore sashes reading "Liberty to Slaves." Four years later, British commander Sir Henry Clinton extended this policy through the Philipsburg Proclamation of June 30, 1779, which promised freedom to any enslaved person in rebel-held territory, regardless of whether they took up arms. Historians estimate that tens of thousands of enslaved African Americans — some put the figure as high as one hundred thousand — sought refuge with British forces over the course of the war as a direct consequence of these two proclamations. This was a policy of the British Empire, not of the colonies rebelling against it.

Southern patriot governments, by contrast, treated the arming and emancipation of enslaved people as a threat rather than a strategy. The most direct test case is the effort of John Laurens, a South Carolina officer and aide to George Washington, who proposed in 1778 that the Continental Congress authorize the recruitment of enslaved men into Continental Army regiments, with freedom granted upon completion of service. Congress approved the concept in March 1779, but only on the condition that the state legislatures of South Carolina and Georgia consent to it. Both refused. Laurens brought the proposal before the South Carolina House of Representatives in 1779, again in 1780, and a final time in 1782, and it was defeated decisively every time, opposed by figures such as Governor John Rutledge and Christopher Gadsden. No regiment was ever raised, and no slave in South Carolina or Georgia was freed under the plan, because the plan never became law. The southern states had the opportunity to adopt an emancipation-for-service policy of their own and declined it repeatedly.

The contrast between British action and southern inaction reveals why the two are so often, and so mistakenly, conflated. Because both the British and figures within the Continental cause floated the idea of freeing enslaved soldiers, popular memory has sometimes collapsed the distinction between a proposal that was debated and rejected by American state governments and a policy that Britain actually implemented on a mass scale. Enslaved people themselves understood the difference at the time: it was toward British lines, not toward Continental Army recruiters, that tens of thousands fled seeking liberty. The historian Cassandra Pybus and others have described this movement as one of the largest self-emancipations in American history prior to the Civil War, and it happened because of British, not American, promises. The southern states' rejection of the Laurens plan was not an aberration but consistent with their broader unwillingness to disturb the institution of slavery even under wartime pressure.

In sum, the historical evidence does not support the claim that the thirteen colonies, or the southern colonies specifically, offered freedom to enslaved people who fought in the Revolutionary War. That offer came from the British Crown through Dunmore's and Clinton's proclamations, and it was British forces, not American ones, who received the enslaved people who acted on it. When a comparable proposal was raised within the American camp, southern legislatures rejected it more than once rather than enact it. Any account that credits the revolutionary colonies with offering slaves their freedom in exchange for service inverts the actual historical roles of the two belligerents in this particular chapter of the war.

text:
“MY FEED. MY WAY” OR CANBERRA’S WAY?

Anthony Albanese and Anika Wells want to force X, Instagram and every other platform to offer you a choice: algorithm slop, or only accounts you follow.

They’re calling it choice.

Then they attach a Digital Duty of Care that lets the Minister or the eSafety Commissioner designate new categories of “harm” whenever they like.

Wells says this is just like safety standards for cars and toasters.

She also says the power already exists, that nobody disallowed YouTube being dragged in, and that if Coalition or One Nation object they must want Parliament recalled “every time there’s a new Grok.”

She even floated using it to declare “nudifying photos of teenagers in bikinis” a new serious harm.

Greens say the bill doesn’t go far enough. 

They want enforced time limits and a ban on autoplay so you can’t “doom scroll.”

So the sales pitch is “genuine and enduring choice.”

The fine print is: platforms must police content, kids’ apps and chatbots get tighter rules, and a minister or commissioner can keep adding new harms, subject only to a 15 day Senate disallowance.

Coalition and One Nation call it a censorship risk.

Wells calls it a global reckoning for big tech.

One of those framings is doing a lot of work.

Read the exposure draft before you cheer “choice.”

The Prompt

# Skin Care Header - Natural

A full-width, editorial-style skincare hero header for a natural/organic cosmetics brand, built in React with framer-motion, featuring oversized split-word display typography ("Natural / Glow ... Shines") with a continuously shimmering "Glow" word and a large autoplaying water/mask video with a floating product card.

## Tech stack
- React (client component, "use client").
- framer-motion — all entrance animations, letter staggers, shimmer loop, and hover micro-interactions.
- No icon library; all icons are inline SVG (hamburger, curved arrow).

## Fonts & global styles
- Import via Google Fonts:
  - `Big Shoulders Display` weights 400, 600, 700 (used for all big display words and the product card heading/button).
  - `Inter` weights 400, 500, 600, 700 (used for body copy, review text, bottom tagline).
- `<link href="https://t.co/1WGeva1MsT" rel="stylesheet" />`
- Page background `#FCFCFD`, base text `#000`. Text selection color: background `#B9F33F`, text black (`selection:bg-[#B9F33F] selection:text-black`). Apply `antialiased`.

## Section container
- Outer wrapper: `w-full min-h-screen bg-[#FCFCFD]`, padding `py-6 px-4 md:px-8 lg:px-12`, `flex flex-col items-center`.
- Inner constraint: `w-full max-w-[1520px] flex flex-col gap-[10px]`.

## Structure, section by section

### 1. Top navigation bar
- `w-full flex justify-between items-center pt-2`.
- Left cluster (`flex items-center gap-3`):
  - Three overlapping circular avatars: `flex items-center -space-x-3 overflow-hidden p-0.5`. Each img is 36×36px, `border-radius: 50%`, `object-fit: cover`, 2px solid white border. Sources (Unsplash portraits): `photo-1534528741775-53994a69daeb`, `photo-1507003211169-0a1dd7228f2d`, `photo-1494790108377-be9c29b29330` (all `?auto=format&fit=crop&w=120&q=80`).
  - Review text: `23K User Glow with Confidence` — Inter 400, 16px, color `#000000`, normal line-height.
- Right: square menu button, 36×36px, `border-radius: 8px`, background `#B9F33F`, no border. Contains a 3-line hamburger SVG (20×20, viewBox 0 0 24 24, stroke `#000000`, strokeWidth 2.5, round caps/joins).

### 2. Hero typography + image grid (`flex flex-col gap-0`)

**Row 1** (`flex flex-col lg:flex-row justify-between items-start gap-2 lg:gap-4`):
- Left: huge word `Natural` in an `<h1>` with `tracking-tighter`, Big Shoulders Display 700, `font-size: clamp(80px, 22vw, 344.248px)`, `line-height: 0.9`, `letter-spacing: -6.885px`, color `#000000`, margin 0. Rendered as individual `inline-block` spans for letter-by-letter stagger.
- Right: image `https://t.co/IerSCtI1qr`, 453×350px, `border-radius: 12px`, `object-cover object-top`, `max-width: 100%`, subtle `shadow-sm`. Container `w-full lg:w-auto flex justify-end`.

**Row 2** (`flex flex-col lg:flex-row items-start lg:items-center justify-between gap-6 lg:gap-4`):
- Left: word `Glow` — Big Shoulders Display 700, `clamp(70px, 17vw, 260px)`, `line-height: 0.9`, `letter-spacing: -5.2px`, base color `#D2D2D2`. Inner span runs a looping shimmer (see animations).
- Middle: paragraph, `width: 349px; max-width: 100%`, Inter 500, 18px, `line-height: 24px`, color `#353534`, left-aligned, `self-center`. Text: `We're committed to helping you achieve radiant, healthy skin. Our expert team offers personalized treatments.`
- Right: word `Shines` — Big Shoulders Display 700, `clamp(80px, 21vw, 334px)`, `line-height: 0.9`, `letter-spacing: -6.68px`, color `#000000`, letter-by-letter stagger.

**Row 3** (`flex flex-col sm:flex-row items-start sm:items-center justify-start gap-6 pb-6`):
- Left tagline: Inter 500, 20px, `line-height: 24px`, color `#626262`, `white-space: pre-line`. Text (two lines): `Expert Skincare Solutions` / `For Healthier, Radiant Skin`.
- Right: pill CTA button. `display: inline-flex; padding: 12px 12px 12px 18px; align-items: center; gap: 9px; border-radius: 12px; background: #B9F33F; border: none; shadow-sm`. Label span Big Shoulders Display 600, 18px, `line-height: 18px`, uppercase, color `#252525` — text toggles between `ORDER YOUR NOW` and `ADDED TO CART` on click (stateful `ordered`). Curved arrow SVG (18×18, viewBox 0 0 24 24, stroke `#252525`, strokeWidth 2.5) with two paths `M7 17L17 7` and `M7 7h10v10`.

### 3. Large media container
- Wrapper: `relative w-full overflow-hidden shadow-sm`, `max-width: 1480px`, `aspect-ratio: 1480/730`, `min-height: 380px`, `max-height: 730px`, `border-radius: 24px`. Parent `w-full flex justify-center pt-2`.
- Autoplaying muted looped video (`object-cover rounded-[24px]`): source `https://t.co/mTSmC81wjt` (type video/mp4). Poster: the header sm image PNG above.
- Floating white product card, absolutely positioned `top-6 left-6 md:top-10 md:left-10`, hidden below `sm` (`hidden sm:flex`), `flex-col justify-between`, `bg-white/95 backdrop-blur-md`, 280×210px, `border-radius: 20px`, `p-5`, `shadow-lg`, `border border-black/5`, `z-10`.
  - Top row: pill badge `SPECIAL CARE` (`text-[10px] font-bold tracking-widest uppercase bg-[#E3FE98] text-[#242020] px-2.5 py-1 rounded-full`) + rating `★ 4.9` (`text-xs font-semibold text-amber-500`).
  - Middle: `<h3>` `BIOMOS SLEEPING MASK` (Big Shoulders Display, `text-xl font-extrabold uppercase text-[#242020] leading-tight`), then paragraph `Plant-based formula infused with organic alpine moss & squalane for intense overnight hydration.` (`text-[14px] text-[#242020]/80 mt-1 leading-snug`).
  - Bottom row: `border-t border-black/10 pt-2`, left `100% Organic` (`font-bold text-[#4C5B45] text-[12px]`), right Shop Now button toggling to `Added ✓` with an arrow `→` that slides right on hover (`group-hover:translate-x-0.5 transition-transform`).

## Assets — every URL
- Header small image: `https://t.co/IerSCtI1qr`
- Hero video: `https://t.co/mTSmC81wjt`
- Avatars: `https://t.co/Fj5f22MQr1`, `https://t.co/rLdzqEMq38`, `https://t.co/V90uTy4vmD`

## Animations (all whileInView, viewport once: true)
- Shared entrance easing: cubic-bezier `[0.16, 1, 0.3, 1]`.
- Headline stagger: container variants stagger children 0.08s. "Natural" uses `delayChildren` 0 (custom={0}); "Shines" uses `delayChildren` 0.48 (custom={0.48}). Letter variant: from `{opacity:0, y:50}` to `{opacity:1, y:0}` over 1.1s.

```jsx
const letterVariants = {
  hidden: { opacity: 0, y: 50 },
  visible: { opacity: 1, y: 0, transition: { duration: 1.1, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1] } },
};
```

- Avatars: container `staggerChildren: 0.18, delayChildren: 0.9`; each item from `{opacity:0, scale:0.75}` to `{opacity:1, scale:1}` over 0.9s.
- Review text: from `{opacity:0, x:-10}` to `{opacity:1, x:0}`, 0.7s, delay 0.95.
- "Glow" block enters `{opacity:0, y:30}`→`{opacity:1, y:0}`, 1.1s, delay 0.95. Inner span runs an infinite shimmer:

```jsx
<motion.span animate={{
  color: ['#D2D2D2', '#F0F0F0', '#D2D2D2'],
  textShadow: [
    '0 0 0px rgba(255,255,255,0)',
    '0 0 20px rgba(255,255,255,0.6)',
    '0 0 0px rgba(255,255,255,0)',
  ],
}} transition={{ duration: 3.5, repeat: Infinity, ease: 'easeInOut', delay: 1.8 }} />
```

- Middle paragraph: `{opacity:0, y:15}`→`{opacity:1, y:0}`, 1.2s, delay 1.05.
- Top-right image: `{opacity:0, scale:1.12}`→`{opacity:1, scale:1}`, 1.6s, delay 0.95.
- Bottom tagline: `{opacity:0, y:15}`→`{opacity:1, y:0}`, 0.9s, delay 1.15.
- CTA button: enters `{opacity:0, scale:0.8}`→`{opacity:1, scale:1}`, spring (stiffness 180, damping 22), delay 1.2. `whileHover="hover"` scales label to 1.03 and translates arrow `x:3, y:-3` (0.2s easeOut); `whileTap` scale 0.95. Menu button hover scale 1.05, tap 0.95.
- Large video container: `{opacity:0, scale:1.04}`→`{opacity:1, scale:1}`, 0.8s, delay 0.2.
- Overlay card: `{opacity:0, y:15}`→`{opacity:1, y:0}`, 0.7s, delay 0.4.

## Responsive behavior
- `sm` (~640px): Row 3 switches from column to row; overlay product card becomes visible (`hidden sm:flex`).
- `md` (~768px): outer padding increases (`md:px-8`); overlay card offset grows to `md:top-10 md:left-10`.
- `lg` (~1024px): Rows 1 & 2 switch to horizontal layout (`lg:flex-row`), Row 2 aligns items center; `lg:px-12`; the top-right image stops being full width (`lg:w-auto`).
- Display type scales fluidly via `clamp()` on every big word so it shrinks on mobile and caps on desktop.

## Key design principles
- Oversized editorial display type with tight negative letter-spacing and 0.9 line-height dominates the composition.
- Signature accent color `#B9F33F` (lime) for the CTA and menu button; softer `#E3FE98` badge.
- The "Glow" word is intentionally light gray (`#D2D2D2`) with a subtle looping glow to read as a background/ghost word.
- Motion is choreographed with escalating delays (~0.9–1.2s) so the hero assembles in a deliberate sequence.
- Natural/organic feel via water video and plant-based copy.

## Common mistakes to avoid
- Do not drop the letter-by-letter split — each big word renders as individual inline-block spans.
- Keep the "Glow" shimmer infinite and subtle; do not make it a one-time animation.
- Preserve exact clamp() font sizes and negative letter-spacing values, or the layout balance breaks.
- Keep the video muted + playsInline so autoplay works on mobile; always set the poster fallback.
- Do not remove `viewport={{ once: true }}` — animations should not replay on re-scroll.

## Page title
Skin Care Header - Natural

text:
Grok's take on the Australian government's latest Orwellian masterpiece. @mattjcan 
The last line "That is not how power works. That is how power accumulates."

"The Albanese government just dropped the exposure draft of its Digital Duty of Care. Official line: “basic safety standards for the online products we use every day,” plus the cuddly “My Feed, My Way” slogan. Translation: a statutory obligation, enforced by the eSafety Commissioner with fines north of $109 million, that tells almost the entire internet stack to take “reasonable steps” so far as “reasonably practicable” to deliver a “safe online environment for all Australians.”

That last phrase should make anyone who has ever read a statute reach for the whisky.

What it actually does
It is not a narrow “take down CSAM and terrorist videos” rule. The issues paper and today’s announcement put the duty across the full tech stack: social media, messaging apps, games, dating services, porn sites, generative AI and chatbots, hosting providers, ISPs, search engines, app stores, and even equipment and operating systems (phones, tablets, wearables, the OS itself).

Core requirements include:
- Annual (or on-change) risk assessments.
- Mitigation strategies that must consider the “best interests of the child.”
- Safety of algorithms, AI generation systems, and bot accounts.
- Documentation and reporting to eSafety.
- Specific protection for under-18s from content that promotes eating disorders, “hostile ideas about women and gender equality,” pornography, glorification of crime or life-endangering stunts, and serious mental-health distress.

The Minister can designate extra categories of harm by disallowable instrument. eSafety gets streamlined removal powers, including for “nudify” apps.

Some of the listed harms are real and ugly. Child sexual exploitation material, suicide instruction, non-consensual deepfakes, and grooming are not free-speech hills worth dying on. A focused, tightly drafted duty limited to clearly illegal material would be a different conversation.

This is not that conversation.

The overreach machine
1. “Harm” is a blank cheque.
“Safe online environment,” “seriously harmful threat to public safety,” and “hostile ideas about women and gender equality” are not legal terms of art. They are political weather vanes. Today’s gender-critical post is tomorrow’s “hostile idea.” Yesterday’s abandoned misinformation bill is tomorrow’s “public safety” category added by ministerial instrument. The government even admits the Minister can expand the list of harms without a new Act.

That is how you smuggle viewpoint regulation through the children’s-safety door.

2. Scope is comically vast.
Once you regulate the OS, the ISP, the app store, the search engine *and* the chatbot, you are no longer regulating “platforms.” You are regulating the pipes. Apple, Google, Microsoft, Telstra, OpenAI and a two-person Discord server all sit under the same conceptual duty, differentiated only by the magic words “proportionate to risk.” In practice, the big players will hire lawyers and the small ones will either over-censor or leave the Australian market.

3. Over-compliance is the rational strategy.
A $109 million civil penalty plus “reasonably practicable” plus vague psychosocial harms produces one predictable outcome: platforms will delete first and litigate never. The UK Online Safety Act has already shown how this works — extra-legal blocking, smaller sites disappearing, and “safety” teams treating political speech as a compliance risk. Australia is copying the model while adding extra moral categories.

4. Surveillance is not optional.
To “prevent, monitor and address” harms from bots, anonymous accounts, coordinated inauthentic activity and algorithmic amplification, companies need more identity signals, more logging, more content scanning. Critics have already flagged the risk of a digital-ID-by-stealth regime even if the government swears it will not demand a driver’s licence at the login screen. Anonymity is not a luxury for whistleblowers, domestic-violence victims or people who simply do not want every opinion attached to their real name.

5. One regulator with a history.
eSafety already operates a large informal-notice practice that has drawn court criticism. Giving that office broader systemic powers, audit-at-the-company’s-expense authority, and a mandate to police “safety of features” is an invitation to mission creep. Informal pressure plus formal fines is how speech regulation actually happens, not via High Court test cases.

6. “My Feed, My Way” is not the freedom it pretends to be.
Forcing platforms to offer a non-algorithmic default is, on its face, a user-empowerment measure. In combination with the rest of the duty it becomes something else: the government is now in the business of designing the architecture of attention. The same regulator that can tell you what content is too “hostile” can also decide whether the chronological feed is being offered in good faith.

The Orwellian texture
It is not 1984 because there is no Ministry of Truth stamping books. It is more like a Ministry of Safety that never has to prove a single post caused a single harm — only that a company failed to take “reasonable steps” against a foreseeable risk of an expanding list of psychosocial injuries.

The language is parental: best interests of the child, safety by design, world-leading protections. The mechanism is infrastructural. Once the state can require risk assessments of *how an operating system or a search index or a language model works*, the Overton window for further intervention shrinks. Future governments of any colour inherit the toolkit.

Combine it with the under-16 social-media ban and age-assurance systems already in train and you get a layered identity-and-compliance architecture sitting over ordinary adult speech. That is the part that feels less “car safety standards” and more “we will decide which thoughts are too sharp for the feed.”

None of this requires assuming cartoon villainy. Bureaucrats respond to incentives. Vague duties + huge fines + political salience of “the children” = ratchet. The ratchet only turns one way.

A serious online-safety regime would name specific, objectively defined illegal harms, keep adult political speech out of the child-protection bucket, put tight limits on ministerial expansion, require actual evidence of systemic failure before the $100 million hammer comes out, and accept that some ugly speech is the price of an open network. This draft does the opposite: it starts with an almost unlimited duty and then promises to be “proportionate” later.

That is not how power works. That is how power accumulates."

[MV Core Tech Fund-I] [IN/AIF2/20-21/0801]

We congratulate @GalaxEye on becoming the 1st Indian spacetech startup to be granted a United States patent for satellite imaging technology.

What the patent covers:
The patent protects GalaxEye’s proprietary OptoSAR technology which enables simultaneous all-weather, day-and-night Earth observation from optical and SAR sensors.

GalaxEye's OptoSAR is a single-satellite payload that operates a Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) sensor and a multispectral imager on one optical bench. Because both instruments are physically co-located, they observe the same scene at the same instant from the same viewing angle. Onboard and ground-based AI models then perform sub-pixel co-registration and jitter correction, so the two sensor streams are delivered as a single aligned dataset.

The conventional approach requires two satellites, one carrying SAR and one carrying an optical payload. That introduces parallax from the difference in viewing angle and a temporal gap from the difference in capture time. Neither error can be fully removed in post-processing.

The patented architecture eliminates both at the point of capture.

Why it matters:
Optical imagery is easy to interpret but unusable at night or through cloud and smoke. SAR penetrates all three but is difficult to read. Applications that depend on both — defence, disaster response, insurance assessment, agriculture — have had to accept a margin of uncertainty when combining them. OptoSAR removes that trade-off within a single pass.

The US patent gives GalaxEye a protected position in the jurisdiction where a substantial share of global defence and enterprise demand sits.

As GalaxEye's @thesuyashsingh noted, the technology allows GalaxEye to offer weather-agnostic imaging to global markets across defence, agriculture, insurance and disaster response.

Congratulations again to Suyash Singh, Denil Chawda, Kishan Thakkar, Pranit Mehta, Rakshit Bhatt and the entire GalaxEye team. We are proud to be investors in the company.

✨ BACH BARAS 2026: 5 SACRED RITUALS TO PROTECT YOUR CHILDREN & UNLOCK FAMILY PROSPERITY ✨

Today is Bach Baras (Govatsa Dwadashi) — the blessed day of Gau Mata and her calf. This festival is considered especially powerful for the long life of children, protection from sudden illness, and filling the home with nourishment, stability, and grace.

1️⃣ Gau-Bachda Tilak & Aarti  
Wake early, bathe, and worship a cow with her calf (or a picture/idol pair). Apply roli-tilak, offer a garland, light incense and a diya, and pray at their feet. Chant “Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya” or simply “Gau Mata Ki Jai.” This invites the protective energy of Krishna’s Gocharan Leela into the family. 🐄✨

2️⃣ Bajra Roti & Sprouted Grains Offering  
Prepare thick bajra roti, soaked chana, moth beans, and sprouted moong. Offer these with jaggery and fresh green fodder to Gau Mata and her calf. Wheat and cow’s milk products are traditionally avoided today — the milk belongs to the bachda. This offering is believed to nourish both the child’s health and the family’s fortune. 🌾🙏

3️⃣ Flower & Milk Worship  
Decorate the cow and calf with flowers, pour a little raw milk mixed with Gangajal near their feet (or before the idol), and perform aarti with full devotion. Recite the Bach Baras katha if possible. This simple, clean ritual is said to dissolve hidden fears around children’s well-being and future. 🪔🌸

4️⃣ Seva & Green Fodder Donation  
Donate bajra, jaggery, green fodder, or a simple meal to a gaushala, temple, or a needy family. Serving Gau Mata through seva is considered one of the most direct ways to remove obstacles from a child’s path and bring ease into the home. 🖤🐄

5️⃣ The Shield Mantra  
Chant or listen to “Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya” (108 times) along with a simple prayer to Gau Mata. Combined with Bach Baras energy, it turns parental worry into protection, discipline, and quiet breakthroughs for the whole family. 📖🕉️

🚀 Pro-Tip: Gau Mata and her calf love purity, softness, and non-violence. Today speak gently, avoid harming any creature, keep a vow of honesty, and feed the needy with millet, rice, or sweets. True blessing on Bach Baras comes when outer ritual meets inner tenderness — toward the child in your home and the child in every heart.

text:
📜 HOOK & AUTHENTIC QUOTE

"We are suffocating among people who think too much, yet we are starving for depth. We have engineered a world where distraction is currency and our attention is the commodity traded to keep the machine alive." 

Wait. Franz Kafka didn’t write that exact sentence in 1920. But in his diaries, he wrote something far more chilling:

"You need not leave your room. Remain sitting at your table and listen. You need not even listen, simply wait, just learn to be quiet and alone. The world will freely offer itself to you to be unmasked, it has no choice, it will roll in ecstasy at your feet."

Kafka imagined isolation as a path to truth. A century later, we took his advice—we stayed in our rooms, glued to our desks, staring at screens—but instead of truth, the world offered us an infinite scroll. 

⚡ THE MODERN MIRROR

Kafka envisioned the quiet room as a sanctuary for the soul. Today, that same room is a panopticon of our own making. 

We wake up, bypass the physical world, and immediately open digital portals. We trade the rich, messy reality of existence for algorithmic dopamine hits. We are not forced into prisons of stone and iron; we have willingly constructed digital cages, painting the bars with bright notifications, infinite feeds, and the illusion of connection. 

We sit alone in our rooms, but the world doesn’t roll at our feet in ecstasy. Instead, we roll in exhaustion at the feet of algorithms, feeding our attention to invisible masters.

🧠 DEEP ANALYSIS

1. The Industrialization of Inner Peace
Kafka’s quiet room required stillness. The modern attention economy has commercialized stillness out of existence. Every micro-moment of boredom—the elevator ride, the red light, the pause before sleep—has been colonized. Silicon Valley realized that an empty mind is a dangerous thing for capitalism, so they filled the void with manufactured urgency.

2. The Illusion of Omnipresence
We suffer from FOMO (Fear Of Missing Out), but the deeper affliction is the terror of being irrelevant. By staying perpetually logged in, we believe we are participating in the global conversation. In reality, we are mere spectators in a colosseum where our own attention is the blood being spilled for entertainment. 

3. The Death of Deep Work
Kafka needed solitude to birth masterpieces like *The Metamorphosis*. Today, sustained focus is treated like a rare luxury. The attention economy fragments our consciousness into 15-second intervals, systematically destroying our capacity for deep thought, nuance, and genuine introspection. We know everything about everyone, yet we understand nothing.

4. The Paradox of Solitary Crowds
We have never been more globally connected and locally isolated. Kafka’s solitude was about tuning out the noise to hear the self. Modern digital addiction is about drowning out the self with noise, terrified of what we might hear if the screen finally goes dark.

💡 THE PHILOSOPHICAL TAKEAWAY

Kafka’s prophecy was half-right. The world does come to us in our rooms, but it doesn't reveal its secrets—it demands our surrender. 

Digital addiction isn't a failure of willpower; it is a structural assault on human consciousness. To reclaim our humanity, we don't need a digital detox or a productivity hack. We need a radical rebellion of the mind. 

We must learn, once again, how to sit in an empty room, embrace the discomfort of silence, and remember what it feels like to belong to ourselves rather than the feed. 

#Philosophy #AttentionEconomy #DigitalDetox #Kafka #DeepWork #Mindfulness

text:
✨ BACH BARAS 2026: 5 VEDIC REASONS WE DON’T CUT VEGETABLES — AND EAT SIMPLE RICE & CHICKPEAS ✨

On Bach Baras the kitchen itself becomes a prayer. Sharp blades stay closed. Food stays whole. Here is why Jyotish and the old vrat-niyam treat this day as a “no-cut, no-himsa” fast for the child’s life-span.

1️⃣ Knife carries Mangal (Mars) — cutting energy  
In Vedic astrology a blade is Mars: heat, severance, sudden cuts. Bach Baras is a day for Ayush — long life of the child (the “bachda”). Using a knife on food is seen as inviting the same cutting vibration into the child’s chart. Whole rice and whole chickpeas need no blade, so Mangal stays calm. 🔪➡️🕊️

2️⃣ The calf and the child share one karma-thread  
The festival worships Gau Mata *with* her calf. The folk katha says a woman once cut the calf by mistake; the vrat restored its life. From that day, anything “cut” is treated as a symbolic wound to the bachda. Eating uncut chickpeas and simple rice keeps that thread of life intact. 🐄👶

3️⃣ Dwadashi after Janmashtami is a Krishna–Chandra day  
Bach Baras falls on Krishna Paksha Dwadashi, just after Janmashtami. Moon rules the mind and the child; Krishna rules protection and ahimsa. Cutting vegetables is subtle himsa. Soothing, whole foods (rice + chana) keep Chandra soft and the home’s emotional field safe for children. 🌙🕉️

4️⃣ Sharp instruments create “Chedan Dosha” on a protection tithi  
Jyotish treats pointed tools as agents of chedan — splitting, delay, accidents. On a day meant to remove obstacles from a child’s path, even kitchen cutting is paused. Soaked chickpeas, whole rice, and foods broken by hand carry no chedan; they feed without “cutting” luck. 🌑🙏

5️⃣ Chickpeas and simple rice are sattvic, grounding graha-foods  
Chana is linked to Saturn’s discipline and Jupiter’s nourishment — slow, whole, protective. Plain rice is sattvic anna that does not demand violence in preparation. Together they keep the kitchen tamas-free, so the day’s Gau-puja can actually land as health, study-success, and family stability. 🍚🫘

🚀 Pro-Tip: If you must prepare food, break sprouts and soft veggies by hand. Offer soaked chickpeas and a simple rice or millet preparation to Gau Mata first. The real remedy is not the plate — it is the vow: today we will not cut what we pray to protect.

Kimi Antonelli won Sunday’s Italian Grand Prix with team-mate George Russell P2.

It was a thrilling drive from Kimi as he charged through the field from P19 to become the first Italian to win their home race since Ludovico Scarfiotti in 1966.

It also marks Mercedes 250th Grand Prix victory as a power unit manufacturer and the marque’s eighth victory at Monza; it’s first since 2018 at the ‘Temple of Speed’.

Starting out of position, Kimi started on the Hard tyre but was able to change to the Medium compound under an early race red flag. By that point, he had already gained seven places to run P12.

The Austrian Grand Prix is a classic, and might just be held at one of the most picturesque track on the F1 calendar. Set in the Styrian hills, around 700m above sea level, the short track features rapid lap times and plenty of overtaking opportunities.

Despite the Red Bull Ring having the fewest corners of any circuit on the schedule, it's seen many unforgettable moments throughout the years – and, as the name might suggest, is the track that Red Bull calls home.

Let's take a look at just some of the reasons why Austria is so alluring.

Austrian racing heritage

Austria, despite it's relatively small population, has heaps of racing heritage. Triple World Champion Niki Lauda was born in Vienna, winning titles for Ferrari and McLaren, and was a major factor behind Mercedes’ success while helping convince Lewis Hamilton to join the outfit in 2013.

Jochen Rindt was Austria's first champion – the only posthumous F1 title winner, having tragically passed away during his dominant 1970 season. Gerhard Berger, while never taking the title himself, scored 10 wins during his illustrious career.

More recently, the late Austrian entrepreneur Dietrich Mateschitz and former Austrian F1 racer Helmut Marko – in his role as motorsport advisor – played key roles in Red Bull's success, with the team clinching eight Drivers’ and six Constructors’ titles.

When is the 2026 Austrian Grand Prix?

The 2026 Austrian Grand Prix weekend begins on Friday 26 June, with F1 cars hitting the track for the first two Free Practice sessions, before Free Practice 3 and Qualifying take place on Saturday 27 June. The Grand Prix itself is on Sunday 28 June, at 1500 local time.

News via

Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One

Kimi Antonelli won Sunday’s Italian Grand Prix with team-mate George Russell P2.

It was a thrilling drive from Kimi as he charged through the field from P19 to become the first Italian to win their home race since Ludovico Scarfiotti in 1966.

It also marks Mercedes 250th Grand Prix victory as a power unit manufacturer and the marque’s eighth victory at Monza; it’s first since 2018 at the ‘Temple of Speed’.

Starting out of position, Kimi started on the Hard tyre but was able to change to the Medium compound under an early race red flag. By that point, he had already gained seven places to run P12.

George meanwhile ran the conventional one-stop from P2 by starting on the Medium and taking the Hard under the red flag, with the clear goal to run to the end on that tyre as he led.

Kimi’s progressed continued once the race restarted and cycled through to battle his team-mate for the lead.

A mid-race Virtual Safety Car gave the team the option of pitting Kimi for a new Medium tyre, with signs suggesting that his original Medium tyre wouldn’t have the life to get to the end of the race.

He rejoined in P6 but made short work of cars ahead; in the final stages he closed the gap to George before making the pass for the lead with three laps left.

Our duo took the flag comfortably ahead of the rest of the field to secure the win, and the 50th for an Italian in F1.

Deputy Technical Director Simone Resta represented the team on the podium at his home race.

The team now leads the Constructors’ Championship by 122 points with Kimi heading the Drivers’ standings by 66 points from his team-mate George.

What makes the Austrian Grand Prix special – and why you should see it

Discover what makes the F1 weekend in Austria unmissable.

The Austrian Grand Prix is a classic, and might just be held at one of the most picturesque track on the F1 calendar. Set in the Styrian hills, around 700m above sea level, the short track features rapid lap times and plenty of overtaking opportunities.

Despite the Red Bull Ring having the fewest corners of any circuit on the schedule, it's seen many unforgettable moments throughout the years – and, as the name might suggest, is the track that Red Bull calls home.

Let's take a look at just some of the reasons why Austria is so alluring.

Austrian racing heritage

Austria, despite it's relatively small population, has heaps of racing heritage. Triple World Champion Niki Lauda was born in Vienna, winning titles for Ferrari and McLaren, and was a major factor behind Mercedes’ success while helping convince Lewis Hamilton to join the outfit in 2013.

Jochen Rindt was Austria's first champion – the only posthumous F1 title winner, having tragically passed away during his dominant 1970 season. Gerhard Berger, while never taking the title himself, scored 10 wins during his illustrious career.

More recently, the late Austrian entrepreneur Dietrich Mateschitz and former Austrian F1 racer Helmut Marko – in his role as motorsport advisor – played key roles in Red Bull's success, with the team clinching eight Drivers’ and six Constructors’ titles.

When is the 2026 Austrian Grand Prix?

The 2026 Austrian Grand Prix weekend begins on Friday 26 June, with F1 cars hitting the track for the first two Free Practice sessions, before Free Practice 3 and Qualifying take place on Saturday 27 June. The Grand Prix itself is on Sunday 28 June, at 1500 local time.

Logos TV

The Church usually does not celebrate the earthly birthday of saints, but rather the day of their birth into heaven. 

The only exceptions are the two greatest saints: the Most Pure Virgin Mary and Saint John the Baptist.

September 8 became the feast of the Nativity of the Most Holy Mother of God also because it falls nine months after the feast of the Immaculate Conception of Mary.

The Gospels record very few details from the life of the Virgin Mary. They say nothing about her birth, her youth, or her dormition, and they do not even mention the names of her righteous parents.

The main source of information about the life of the Mother of God is the apocryphal book The Protoevangelium of James, written around the year 140. 

This text contains mostly popular and legendary accounts of Mary’s birth, childhood, and youth. Its purpose was to glorify Mary, highlighting her descent from the line of David and Aaron, her dedication to God, and her virginity.

According to the Protoevangelium, Joachim and Anna were childless for a long time and suffered greatly because of it. They endured much humiliation from those around them. Yet even in such a painful situation, they remained faithful to God, constantly praying, giving alms, and purifying themselves. They strove to fulfill God’s will in everything and lived this way for more than fifty years.

Tradition says that Joachim once went to offer sacrifice in the Temple of Jerusalem, but he heard harsh words spoken against him. He was told that God did not accept his offering because he had no children, and that he must surely be hiding some secret sin. A man like Joachim, who had tried all his life to live according to God’s will, was deeply wounded by these accusations. Sorrowful, he left the Temple and went into the desert, where he prayed and fasted.

Anna learned of what had happened and began to blame herself, saying that every living creature has offspring, yet she could not give a child to her husband. Just as Joachim prayed, so did Anna. Their prayer was heard, and an angel announced to them that they would have a daughter whom the whole human race would glorify. 

And so it happened: Anna’s barrenness was taken away, and she conceived Mary, the Mother of God.❤️

text:
Let's also look at the actual boundary of the controversy: the request by Shastri Ji was specifically to avoid non-vegetarian food inside the Puja Pandals, the shared, consecrated public spaces. No one was raiding private kitchens or policing what people cooked and ate inside their homes. Yet, the pushback treated this simple spatial boundary as a direct existential attack on their entire culinary identity.

Furthermore, according to authentic Shakta rules, any meat associated with the festival must be Niramish, cooked under severe ritual discipline, entirely free of onion, garlic, or standard commercial processing. It is a rigorous sacrificial rite, not a commercial food court market. Even global, multinational fastfood chains understand the depth of these regional restrictions; during Navratri in the North, they completely re-engineer their entire supply chains to offer strict, onion and garlic free menus to respect local sentiments.

Contrast that corporate discipline with the reality of modern urban pandals. True pasubali (animal sacrifice) has been safely replaced by "symbolic representation," slicing a pumpkin (Kushmanda) or sugarcane to signify the "destruction of ego." Ask yourself: how many pandals today actually practice scriptural, disciplined bali? Virtually none. Yet, after watching a vegetable get cleanly chopped for the camera to satisfy "tradition," crowds immediately march out to the commercial stalls surrounding the pandal to feast on non-consecrated commercial food.

text:
From Elite Revolt to Great-Power State: The Making of Modern Greece

The Greek revolt of 1821 was not, in its origins, a spontaneous uprising of a uniformly persecuted population. It emerged from an organized separatist movement operating through diaspora merchants, professionals, officers and Christian political and landed elites who saw an opportunity to replace Ottoman sovereignty with a political order of their own.

The distinction matters. Christians certainly suffered legal inequalities under Ottoman rule. But the revolution was set in motion by the Filiki Eteria, a secret organization founded not in an oppressed Greek village but in Odessa in 1814. Modern scholarship traces the revolutionary networks through merchants, professionals, officers, officials, local notables and other mobile elites operating across several empires. Research on the Peloponnese similarly shows Christian landed elites assessing the revolution in terms of political opportunity, sovereignty and risk. 

Once launched, the revolt expanded into a much broader war involving peasants, sailors, clergy, armed bands and local communities. But its transformation from rebellion into an independent state was another matter.

Money became crucial.

In 1824, representatives of the revolutionary Greek administration raised a loan in London with a nominal value of £800,000. It was issued at only 59 percent, producing £472,000. In 1825, another nominal £2 million loan was issued at 55.5 percent, producing £1.1 million.

On paper, therefore, revolutionary Greece borrowed £2.8 million.

In reality, only £1.572 million was advanced. Historian Maria Christina Chatziioannou calculates that only about £540,000 was actually sent to Greece, while approximately £1.032 million remained in Britain for various purposes; £683,000 was absorbed through prepaid interest, brokerage, debt operations and related financial arrangements. Greece defaulted on the loans in 1827. 

The financial relationship was already tying the revolutionary administration to London before an internationally recognized Greek state even existed.

Militarily, meanwhile, the revolt was approaching disaster. Ibrahim Pasha’s Egyptian forces intervened on the Ottoman side and recovered large areas. It was at this stage that Britain, France and Russia transformed the conflict.

The Treaty of London of 1827 opened the way for intervention. At Navarino, the combined British, French and Russian fleet destroyed the Ottoman-Egyptian fleet. France subsequently deployed troops in the Peloponnese, while Russia fought the Ottoman Empire directly in the Russo-Turkish War of 1828–29.

The rebellion had now become a Great-Power question.

In 1830, Britain, France and Russia formally recognized an independent Greek state. They did not merely recognize a state created entirely by the insurgents. They also determined its political framework, negotiated its borders and chose the form of its government. The Greek Foreign Ministry itself describes the 1830 London Protocol as the first formal international act recognizing Greece as completely independent. 

Then came perhaps the clearest demonstration of external state-building.

The Great Powers decided that Greece would become a monarchy. After Leopold of Saxe-Coburg declined the throne, Britain, France and Russia selected the 17-year-old Bavarian Prince Otto, son of King Ludwig I of Bavaria, as King of Greece. The Convention of London of 7 May 1832 formally offered him the crown of the newly created state. 

Otto arrived with a Bavarian regency because he was still a minor. The arrangements even provided for a force of up to 3,500 Bavarian troops, armed and paid by the Greek state, to support the new monarchy. 

And again, money accompanied political control.

Britain, France and Russia guaranteed another loan of 60 million francs, each power guaranteeing 20 million. British parliamentary records openly stated that such financial assistance was necessary to establish the new government. Otto accepted the Greek crown under the same general financial conditions previously attached to the proposed monarchy of Leopold. 

Even this money was not simply handed to Greece for reconstruction. Under the 1832 settlement, Greece was required to pay the Ottoman Porte an indemnity of 40 million Turkish piastres for ceded territory—about 11.22 million francs according to contemporary British parliamentary calculations—reducing the amount available for the internal needs of the new kingdom. (Hansard)

The sequence is therefore difficult to reduce to the familiar story of an oppressed population simply rising up, defeating an empire and establishing its own state.

The revolutionary movement originated in organized transnational and elite networks. It expanded into a genuine mass war. When that war was threatened with defeat, foreign powers intervened militarily. London financed the revolutionary administration. Britain, France and Russia destroyed the Ottoman-Egyptian fleet, imposed the diplomatic settlement, recognized the new state, negotiated its boundaries, selected its monarchy, chose a Bavarian prince as king and guaranteed the loans on which the new regime depended.

The Greeks started the revolution but the state that emerged from that revolution was constructed within a political, military and financial framework imposed to a remarkable degree by the Great Powers.

What began as a separatist revolt exploiting the weakness of an empire ended when Britain, France and Russia discovered that a Greek state could serve the European balance of power.

text:
Tuesday morning headlines from #Georgia, 8 September

● Former Prosecutor General Otar Partskhaladze, who is wanted internationally by Georgia on murder charges and currently lives in Russia under the name Otar Romanov-Partskhaladze, will lead the international military unit “Georgievsky” to fight on Russia’s side in the war against Ukraine. Partskhaladze told the Russian state-run TASS news agency that the unit’s name refers to the 1783 Treaty of Georgievsk, which established a Russian protectorate over eastern Georgia. He said he was “ready to help Russia achieve the goals set by its leader”.

● Imprisoned former Prime Minister Irakli Gharibashvili published his sixth public letter, accusing the authorities of “dirty political games” against him. Gharibashvili wrote that he has no connection whatsoever with the opposition United National Movement, founded by fellow imprisoned former President Mikheil Saakashvili. He also sarcastically responded to reports alleging that he is an agent of the “deep state” or France. Addressing Parliament Speaker Shalva Papuashvili, Gharibashvili wrote: “This is not a legal process — it is ruthless political persecution.” He again said he was not fighting against his former allies, writing: “You stabbed me in the back.”

● Leaders of the ruling Georgian Dream party responded to Gharibashvili’s latest letter.

Party secretary-general and Tbilisi Mayor Kakha Kaladze called the former prime minister’s statements unfounded and said it was painful to see his former ally “in the situation he has put himself in”. Asked whether Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze could resign, Kaladze described Kobakhidze as an “honest, decent person” and expressed his support for him.

Kobakhidze, in turn, called Gharibashvili’s letters frivolous. He said the former prime minister had “sunk to the level of a blogger from a peculiar black-and-white newspaper” and described his letters as “absurd and tragic”.

● A contract has been signed in Tbilisi for the design and construction of a tram line. The project has a budget of 287.65 million lari (about $110.5 million). The approximately 7.5-km line, with 11 stops, will connect Didube metro station with Didi Dighomi via the Digomi residential area. The project also includes construction of a tram depot. A separate tender will be announced for the purchase of 10 trams. City Hall warned that construction would cause temporary disruptions and changes to traffic flows, with residents to be informed in advance.

● Cargo transport along the Middle Corridor in Azerbaijan has been delayed for almost a month. A railcar carrying mineral water from Georgia to Uzbekistan has been sitting at Azerbaijan’s Alat port since August 13, waiting for a ferry to cross the Caspian Sea. Paata Tsagareishvili, director of Georgia’s Transport Corridor Research Centre, told BMG that one reason for the delay was priority being given to Azerbaijani cargo. He said such prolonged delays highlight one of the Middle Corridor’s main problems: fast and predictable cargo transportation along the route remains impossible, reducing the corridor’s competitiveness and forcing shippers to seek alternative routes.

● Economy Minister Mariam Kvrivishvili met Abdulaziz Zayed Al Shamsi, regional executive director of Abu Dhabi Ports Group. They discussed the Anaklia deep-sea port and the Tbilisi dry port projects. Abu Dhabi Ports Group is one of the main investors in the Tbilisi dry port. The government has previously said it plans to develop Anaklia under a so-called “landlord port” model, with the state owning the port while investors are offered long-term terminal leases.

● Georgian company Solidus imported around 1,700 tonnes of petrol into Abkhazia in August from territory controlled by the Georgian government, Georgia’s Radio Liberty reports. Of this, 1,175 tonnes was 95-octane petrol and 523 tonnes was 92-octane. Supplies cross the Enguri River bridge and will continue in September. It was previously reported that international company Repsol (Connect) had ended its cooperation with Solidus. It is unclear where the petrol is currently being purchased. Solidus said only that purchases are made in Georgian lari from Georgian suppliers and that the fuel is supplied to Abkhazia for civilian use.

● Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze said the government plans to mobilise around $7 billion by 2032 for the development of Georgia’s transport and logistics infrastructure. Speaking at the Georgian International Maritime Forum in Batumi, he said the 10-year plan envisages doubling the capacity of the country’s railways and ports and tripling the capacity of international airports. Kobakhidze said more than 1 billion lari (about $386 million) would be invested this year in upgrading railway infrastructure and rolling stock. He also said 75% of the East-West International Highway has already been completed.

● The opposition Girchi party is changing its name to the “Free People’s Party”. The party said the existence of two political organisations called Girchi confuses voters and allows opponents to attribute certain positions to the wrong party.

● Incidents were reported in Tbilisi and across Georgia amid worsening weather. A tornado was spotted over the Black Sea near Kobuleti. A landslide on the road to the mountain resort of Gomismta temporarily blocked traffic. Strong winds brought down trees in Tbilisi. No injuries were reported.

text:
This is a phenominal idea—on par with Trump Accounts for children. The government already runs a long list of programs aimed at working mothers: tax credits, childcare subsidies, nutrition aid, and job-protected leave. Those help parents who stay in the labor force. What has been missing is a comparable path for a parent who wants to stay home and raise the kids. If the goal is supporting families—not only supporting employment—then stay-at-home parents should be in the conversation too.

Who these programs apply to (typical criteria)

Child Tax Credit — Parents/guardians with a qualifying child under 17, valid SSNs, and income generally at or below $200k single / $400k joint. 

Child and Dependent Care Credit — Working parents (or looking for work) who pay for care of a child under 13 so they can work. 

Dependent Care FSA — Employees whose employer offers the plan; used for childcare so the parent(s) can work.

CCDF / Texas Child Care Services — Low- to moderate-income parents who are working, in school, or in job training.

Head Start / Early Head Start — Low-income families with children 0–5 (or pregnant women for Early Head Start).

WIC — Pregnant, postpartum, or breastfeeding women and children under 5 who meet income limits.

SNAP / TANF — Low-income households; TANF usually requires work or job-search activity.

EITC — Low- to moderate-income workers with earned income; larger credit if they have qualifying children.

FMLA — Employees who have worked 12 months / 1,250 hours for a covered employer (50+ employees in most private cases). Unpaid, job-protected leave for birth/bonding.

Pregnant Workers Fairness Act / PUMP Act — Covered employees who are pregnant, postpartum, or pumping at work. No income test.

Seopapa’s AI-driven approach aims to address the evolving landscape of SEO by leveraging advanced technology that can adapt quickly to changes in search algorithms. Traditional SEO methods often struggle with rapid updates, but Seopapa promises a more dynamic and responsive solution.

Their proprietary tools use machine learning to analyze current trends and adjust strategies accordingly. This means they can stay ahead of algorithmic shifts and maintain high rankings even as Yandex continues to evolve its criteria for ranking websites.

The service uses proprietary tools to analyze your website's performance and identify areas for improvement. The service does not include manual link building or content creation services beyond what can be automated through their platform. Additionally, Seopapa does not offer direct support for non-Yandex search engines like Google or Bing.
