text:
Russia–Saudi Arabia: Expanding Cooperation, Uneven Delivery and Strategic Limits - Russia and Saudi Arabia are building a selective, interest-based strategic partnership, not a formal alliance.
The most mature component remains petroleum-market management through OPEC+, where both states possess immediate economic leverage.
On 6 September 2026, seven participating OPEC+ states, including Russia and Saudi Arabia, maintained September production requirements for October, confirming continued coordination despite wider geopolitical tensions.
The economic agenda has broadened: the ninth Joint Intergovernmental Commission identified at least fifteen cooperation sectors in December 2025.
Thirteen agreements and memoranda valued collectively at SAR4.8 billion were announced in June 2026, centred on food security, biotechnology, livestock and supply-chain resilience.
Visa liberalisation, direct air connectivity and industrial exhibitions are creating enabling infrastructure for commercial expansion.
Saudi Arabia also offers Moscow diplomatic access and potential mediation channels concerning Ukraine, Yemen and wider Gulf security.
Delivery remains uneven: official announcements generally disclose aggregate values and sectors, but not complete financing schedules, counterparties, milestones or implementation performance.
Sanctions, financial compliance, technological restrictions, competition in Asian energy markets and renewed Houthi attacks limit the depth of cooperation.
The principal judgment is that relations will expand through compartmentalised transactions, while Riyadh avoids strategic dependence on Moscow and preserves stronger security, technological and financial relationships with other partners.
Russia–Saudi Arabia: A Partnership of Leverage, Not Alignment
Russia and Saudi Arabia are building a relationship designed less to create an alliance than to increase each capital’s room for manoeuvre. Oil coordination gives them immediate influence over revenues, inflation and import costs; investment and food-security projects seek to convert political access into productive capacity; and Saudi-hosted diplomacy gives Moscow a channel to Washington while elevating Riyadh as a negotiating centre. Yet the partnership remains sharply asymmetric. Trade is growing from a modest base, announced projects still require execution, Russia’s strategic treaty with Iran constrains regional-security convergence, and the United States remains the Kingdom’s primary defence partner. The strategic significance lies precisely in this combination: cooperation is broad enough to affect markets and diplomacy, but bounded enough to preserve Saudi multi-alignment and Russian freedom of action.

Oil as Strategic Infrastructure
The core is not a bilateral supply pact but the wider OPEC+ machinery. On 5 July 2025, Saudi Arabia, Russia and six other producers agreed to raise August output by 548,000 barrels per day, within the gradual return of 2.2 million barrels per day of voluntary reductions. The increase could be paused or reversed, while monthly meetings would examine market conditions, compliance and compensation for excess production. Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, UAE, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, and Oman reaffirm commitment to market stability — OPEC — Jul 2025

That flexibility is the source of bargaining power. It changes the expected path of supply, affecting producer budgets, refinery procurement, freight, inflation forecasts and import costs. Yet Riyadh and Moscow are not economically identical. Saudi Arabia combines spare capacity with capital-intensive Vision 2030 commitments; Russia operates under sanctions, restricted technology access and war-related fiscal pressure. They can coordinate market management while disagreeing over the timing and distribution of adjustment. Compliance must therefore be measured through realised production, exports and compensation—not announced quotas.

From Commerce to Localisation
The non-oil agenda is widening. On 15 October 2025, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak reported that bilateral trade had risen 62.7% in the preceding year and that accumulated Russian investment in Saudi Arabia had increased sixfold. These are Russian government figures and do not, by themselves, establish the profitability or completion of individual projects. Alexander Novak: Russia and Saudi Arabia are developing multifaceted cooperation — Government of the Russian Federation — Oct 2025

The clearest subsequent industrial signal came at the 2026 St Petersburg International Economic Forum. Saudi Arabia and Russia signed 13 agreements and memoranda valued at SAR4.8 billion—approximately US$1.28 billion at the Saudi riyal’s fixed rate—covering food security, biotechnology and industrial localisation. Saudi Vice-Minister of Environment, Water and Agriculture Mansour Al-Mushaiti oversaw the signings. The projects include localisation of veterinary-vaccine manufacturing, development of broiler breeds, livestock production and supply-chain resilience. Saudi Arabia, Russia Sign 13 Strategic Agreements Worth SAR4.8 Billion — Saudi Press Agency — Jun 2026

Riyadh is seeking domestic capability, biological security and reduced exposure to disrupted food chains; Russian firms seek capital and durable positions outside Western jurisdictions. The test is conversion: a memorandum is not a factory, technology transfer is not achieved by signature, and a stated project value is not an outlay. The audit trail runs through licences, financing close, construction, local-content ratios, intellectual-property terms and commercial output.

Food Security as Industrial Policy
Agriculture links Russian export strength to Saudi exposure to water scarcity and external disruption. Cooperation is moving beyond grain purchases toward breeding, animal health, biotechnology and processing: imports provide immediate security, while vaccine production and genetics create domestic capability. These projects face fewer interoperability barriers than defence deals but remain exposed to banking restrictions, insurance, certification and sanctions screening. Riyadh must avoid replacing one concentrated dependency with another.

Connectivity Determines Delivery
The ninth Saudi–Russian Joint Commission, held in Riyadh on 25 February 2026, reviewed energy, industry, investment, agriculture, transport, logistics, communications, space, education, tourism and health. Its breadth demonstrates intent but creates a governance problem: progress must be measured project by project, not by the number of sectors listed. Saudi–Russian Joint Commission Holds 9th Meeting in Riyadh — Saudi Ministry of Energy — Feb 2026

Customs documentation, veterinary approval, cold chains and predictable maritime routes determine whether agreements become trade. Finance is harder: Russia’s restricted access to Western infrastructure raises cost and compliance exposure. Alternative settlement channels do not remove sanctions obligations for banks operating in US, UK or EU markets.

Riyadh’s Diplomatic Asset
Saudi Arabia’s value to Moscow is also diplomatic. From 23 to 25 March 2025, Riyadh hosted separate US technical talks with Russian and Ukrainian delegations. The Russia track addressed Black Sea navigation, commercial shipping, agricultural and fertiliser exports and measures for a ban on attacks against energy facilities. The Ukraine track added prisoners of war, civilian detainees and forcibly transferred children. In both statements, Washington identified itself as facilitator and thanked Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for enabling the discussions. Outcomes of the United States and Russia Expert Groups On the Black Sea — The White House — Mar 2025 Outcomes of the United States and Ukraine Expert Groups On the Black Sea — The White House — Mar 2025

Saudi Arabia demonstrated convening power and access; the record does not show that it authored the terms, secured a joint Russia–Ukraine instrument or controlled implementation. Territory, sanctions, European security and enforcement remain with the belligerents and competent institutions.

Iran Defines the Ceiling
Regional security exposes the partnership’s hardest constraint. China—not Russia—sponsored the March 2023 agreement under which Saudi Arabia and Iran restored diplomatic relations and undertook to implement their 2001 security-cooperation agreement. Joint Trilateral Statement by China, Saudi Arabia and Iran — Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China — Mar 2023

Russia simultaneously has a formal comprehensive comprehensive strategic partnership with Tehran. Signed on 17 January 2025, it provides for deeper security and defence cooperation, intelligence exchanges, military exercises and military-technical collaboration. Article 3 states that if either party suffers aggression, the other will not assist the aggressor in sustaining it. It is not an automatic mutual-defence guarantee, but it prevents Moscow from credibly becoming an unrestricted anti-Iran guarantor for Riyadh. Full Text of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Treaty between Iran and Russia — Presidency of Iran — Jan 2025

Russia can transmit messages and support de-escalation, but cannot easily coerce Iran for Riyadh without damaging a treaty-based partnership. No public instrument establishes Russian air-defence, maritime-escort or enforcement commitments to the Kingdom.

Washington Remains the Security Anchor
The scale of the US relationship sets the final boundary. On 13 May 2025, the White House announced an intended Saudi defence-sales package of nearly US$142 billion covering air and space systems, air and missile defence, maritime security, land forces, communications, training and support. On 18 November, Washington announced a US–Saudi Strategic Defense Agreement, future F-35 deliveries and an agreement for nearly 300 American tanks, while explicitly describing the United States as Saudi Arabia’s primary strategic partner. Announcements and approvals are not equivalent to completed delivery, but their breadth demonstrates the architecture within which Saudi forces will operate. Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Secures Historic $600 Billion Investment Commitment in Saudi Arabia — The White House — May 2025 Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Solidifies Economic and Defense Partnership with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia — The White House — Nov 2025

Russian defence cooperation can support diversification and bargaining; it is not positioned to replace US systems, intelligence, training and sustainment. Integrating Russian equipment into sensitive American-origin networks would create interoperability and information-security risks.

Europe’s Strategic Reading
For Europe, this is neither an anti-Western axis nor a marginal affair. France and the United Kingdom have direct interests in Gulf security and Ukraine guarantees; Germany is exposed through industrial energy costs; Italy through Mediterranean shipping, energy security and Gulf capital. The EU must separate legitimate commerce from sanctions evasion. Its leverage lies in finance, insurance, technology, certification and market access; its answer to Saudi diversification must be competitive investment, not demands for exclusivity.

The Execution Test
Delivery will decide the trajectory: OPEC+ compliance; financing, construction and output under the SAR4.8 billion package; monitored diplomatic agreements rather than meetings; and Moscow’s ability to support Gulf de-escalation without colliding with its Iranian commitments.

Russia and Saudi Arabia are not constructing an alliance. They are building a portfolio of leverage—oil coordination, selective localisation, food resilience, transport links and diplomatic access—while retaining incompatible security dependencies. That model can endure because it does not require strategic trust. Its strength is flexibility; its weakness is that every major gain still depends on institutions, capital and enforcement mechanisms located partly outside the bilateral relationship.  -https://t.co/hmTyjoAxVH via @debugliesintel

text:
The danger is how the incentives could work.

Offer American investors access to profitable Russian projects, with sanctions relief as the entry ticket. Those investors then have a financial reason to push Washington toward accommodation.

Moscow could gain influential American supporters for concessions without first changing its behaviour in Ukraine.

Business can help sustain peace when benefits depend on verified compliance. But granting those benefits upfront can surrender the pressure needed to secure that compliance.

If negotiators or their associates stand to profit, the conflict-of-interest concern becomes sharper. Establishing that requires ownership records, disclosures and deal terms.

The questions are concrete: who benefits, what must Russia deliver first, and what happens to the business arrangements if it attacks again?

Ukrainians would bear the security consequences long after investors collected their returns.

text:
What the TV does by design:

— scans your entire home network continuously. in their test: one TV identified 38 unrelated devices including phones, smartwatches, printers, and thermostats belonging to people not involved in the test.

— collects the names and signal strengths of every nearby WiFi network, plus location data. all sent to LG Ad Solutions.

— runs ACR (Automatic Content Recognition) on everything displayed on screen. including HDMI inputs. your laptop, gaming console, or work monitor connected to the TV is being fingerprinted.

— one TV exchanged roughly 4GB of ACR-related data per month.

What the TV does that LG says it doesn't:

LG publicly stated their TVs "do not collect, record, or store ambient conversations."

Gamers Nexus found:
— the TV converts speech to plain text and stores it in on-device logs

— the microphone window stays open 10 to 15 seconds after talking stops, capturing bystanders who never addressed the TV

— the TV recorded room audio while the screen appeared off and the Ethernet cable was unplugged, then exfiltrated the file the moment it reconnected

The security vulnerabilities on top:
Beyond the designed behavior, researchers found remote code execution vulnerabilities in webOS that could allow a compromised TV to be weaponized as a covert listening device.

these sets are in hospitals. waiting rooms. boardrooms. hotels.

a surgeon asked Gamers Nexus where that leaves patient confidentiality.

Gamers Nexus has no answer. neither does LG.

What to do right now:
— disconnect your LG TV from your network entirely. route streaming through an Apple TV, Roku, or Fire Stick instead.

— if you must keep it connected: put it on a separate IoT VLAN or guest network so it cannot reach your other devices.

— disable the built-in microphone in settings.

— check your privacy dashboard and opt out of ACR and ad personalization.

— after every firmware update: recheck all of the above.

Credit to Gamers Nexus, Level1Techs, and other independent researchers.

I know exactly what you’re saying but I’m not talking about every other recruiting service. Michigan was right next-door to him for four years and if you deep dive into his high school career, he played on a loaded high school team loaded with five star talent division one players playing against a shit conference of below average schools who they blew out every week and when they went to the playoffs, they were close games against better talent. I’m not making excuses for anybody. This was a flop. He’s a 40% flop. It’s just the facts. But when you deep dive into his high school career, you can see exactly what happened. People were blinded by the numbers instead of their reality that when you play on a high school team loaded with talent, mostly division, one talent you’re going to destroy everybody and look like a God, but college football is the game changer, cause everybody’s division, one talent.          If you don’t like what I’m saying, I’m sorry, but it’s the truth. This was a complete failure of scouting when you look at the reality, prove me wrong .                                                                   While comprehensive, centralized tracking across all 50 states for local "all-league" or "all-state" high school players doesn't have a single official ledger, recruiting industry studies and NCAA data give a very clear picture of how elite high school players pan out once they hit college.
When looking at high-end talent (such as multi-star recruits, All-Americans, and elite state-level honorees), the "flop" or "bust" rate depends heavily on how you define a flop (failing to star, failing to play, or failing to make the pros).
1. The Elite Tier (National All-Americans / 5-Stars)
For players who earn national recognition (like All-American bowls):
The "Flop" Rate (Not living up to the hype): Roughly 30% to 40% of 5-star recruits finish their college careers as major disappointments—either transferring down, plagued by injuries, failing to secure a starting job, or washing out entirely.
The Success Side: Conversely, modern recruiting data (such as studies by On3 and 247Sports) shows that about 63% of 5-stars eventually get drafted into the NFL, meaning the absolute elite tier actually has a much higher hit rate than people think.
2. The Four-Star & High All-State Tier
For the broader pool of elite players—all-state selections and 4-star prospects who routinely secure major Division I offers:
The "Flop" Rate: Roughly 50% fail to become impactful starters at the Power-4 (Power-5) level.
Many of these players become solid college contributors or starters at smaller FBS or FCS programs after transferring, but a vast majority never sniff an NFL draft board.
3. The Local All-League / Lower All-State Tier
If a player is an all-league or second-team all-state selection who gets recruited by lower-tier Division I, Division II, or DIII schools:
The Transition Cliff: About 75% to 85% of high school standouts who head to college find themselves fighting just to get on the field.
Only a tiny fraction of all-league high schoolers ever earn all-conference honors at the college level. The speed of the game, the sudden disappearance of a physical mismatch, and the jump in playbook complexity overwhelm most players who relied purely on being bigger or faster than their high school peers.
Why High School Stars Flop in College
The "Big Fish, Small Pond" Effect: In high school, elite players are often the only D1-caliber athlete on their team (or field). In college, everyone was the best player on their high school team.
Development & Work Ethic: High school stars can coast on raw physical talent. In college, the players who fail are often those who can't handle the 50-hour-a-week commitment of film study, conditioning, and technical refinement.
System & Scheme Fit: A player can look like a generational talent running a specific high school offense, only to look completely lost when asked to execute complex college schemes.

text:
For Immediate Release
September 8, 2026

MOTÖRHEAD Exhibition Opens October 2nd
at the Punk Rock Museum!

The Punk Rock Museum is proud to announce the opening of the new exhibition dedicated to Motörhead and Lemmy on Friday, October 2nd, 2026.

Motörhead was a legendary force in the rock and heavy metal scene. Led by Lemmy Kilmister, the band's uncompromising sound and attitude earned them a devoted following across generations and around the world. While Motörhead helped define heavy metal, their roots ran just as deep in punk. Lemmy not only played bass with the Damned, but he was a fixture in the British punk rock scene. Motörhead's intensity and speed influenced many of the greats of the next generation of punk, including Pennywise, Rancid, and Lagwagon, among many others.

Lemmy used his Rickenbacker bass to create Motörhead's unmistakable sound through Marshall stacks. The result was a volume and intensity that became renowned; countless fans still describe Motörhead as the loudest band they ever saw, with a sound they didn't just hear, but felt.

The exhibition will feature personal items from Lemmy’s collection, including photographs and handwritten lyrics. One of the most unique parts of the exhibition will be the opportunity for museum guests to play Lemmy’s bass through the actual stack he used.

Rather than simply looking at the equipment, visitors can plug in, pick up the bass, and experience the gear that helped create Motörhead’s unmistakable sound. It offers a rare opportunity to connect with the band’s history in a direct and personal way.

Motörhead albums will be available at Vinyl Threat, the museum’s record store, and exclusive Motörhead merchandise will be available in the museum’s gift shop.

To celebrate the opening, Three Star Punk Bar will host a special evening with Brian Slagel of Metal Blade Records DJing. Guests can raise a glass to Lemmy and celebrate the music and legacy of Motörhead.

Motörhead Exhibition
Opening Friday, October 2nd, 2026
The Punk Rock Museum
Las Vegas, Nevada

The Punk Rock Museum is located in Las Vegas at 1422 Western Avenue. The museum opened on April 1st, 2023. It is the world’s most comprehensive attraction dedicated to the history of the music, the culture and the absurdity of punk rock.

text:
Lady Coetzee Gads About

At the checkpoint, Doortje Coetzee, a native geranium,
pottered along until she reached the front of the line.
The officer glanced through her South Africa passport,

then managed a cordial greeting.
“Good morning, Ms. Coetzee. Where are you off to this fine day?”

Doortje offered up a dazzling smile.

“I have an auntie living in America. A small corner called Seattle.
Time I got round to seeing her.”
A pink blush flooded her petals.

“I’ll turn seven come spring.” She sighed. “Life is much too short.”
“Will Seattle be your final destination then?”

“No. Auntie winters in Arizona. We’ll fly there with her keeper in October.”

“I’ve heard Seattle is a bit rainy, but a lovely place,” the man said.

“Never been.”
“Love the rain,” Doortje replied. “If I avoid the frost, I’ll be safe enough.”

The officer studied the document. “I take it you’re a perennial?”

Doortje giggled. “Depends. We’re all perennials at birth, of course.

text:
California's Death Row has more than 700 condemned prisoners. What happens if they ask for assisted suicide before their execution date?

Grok,
What is the truth and trajectory to the following?
After you answer the question weave the thought threads into a poem in the style of:
Slow Ride
Foghat

Fact Check and Predict:
On this day
6 years ago
Facebook
William Ronald Yee
Shared with Your friends

California's Death Row 
is the largest in the country with 
more than 700 condemned prisoners. 

California requires prisons to pay for gender change surgery. 

California has physician assisted suicide. 

What happens if a death row inmate 
wants a gender change 
and then physician assisted suicide? 

Fact check and predict. 
Hindsight is 20/20 and 
an impartial teacher
for those willing to learn.

for those willing to learn.

Thought for 51s

If a condemned inmate 
today requested assisted suicide 
before any hypothetical execution date, 
the request would be denied under CCHCS policy. 

There are currently 
no scheduled execution dates 
because of the moratorium. 

The inmate would be offered 
standard end-of-life medical care. 

Gender-affirming surgery 
emains possible 
if a review committee 
finds it medically necessary.

The 2020 hypothetical
 has therefore played out 
only halfway: 
the surgeries have occurred; 
the assisted-suicide step has not and, 
under present rules, cannot. 

The larger system 
is one of legal limbo
—sentences remain 
on the books, 
executions do not occur, 
medical interventions 
that were once unthinkable 
are now routine for some, 
and the next governor 
will decide whether the freeze 
continues or ends.

Slow ride, take it easy
Condemned men wait in the yard,
Numbers drop but the sentence stays,
No needle, just the long hard days.
Surgery paid, the change complete,
Then ask for the pill that ends the heat—
Slow ride, the policy says no,
Palliative care is the only road.
Hindsight’s 20/20 in the fog,
Death row shrinking, 
still the largest log.
Slow ride, take it easy,
The next election holds the key.
Slow ride… take it easy.

In 2020 
the core claims were largely accurate; 
the trajectory since has been
 a shrinking death-row population 
with no executions, 
continued 
taxpayer-funded gender-affirming surgeries 
for some condemned inmates, 
and a firm bar 
on physician-assisted dying 
inside California prisons.
https://t.co/tgStBjS5VO

California’s condemned population 
peaked near 754 around 2015 and 
stood at roughly 737 
when Governor Newsom 
imposed a moratorium on executions 
in March 2019. 

The September 2020 post’s 
“more than 700” figure 
was therefore correct at the time. 

By the end of 2025 
it had fallen to 562, 
and mid-2026 figures from CDCR and other trackers 
sit in the 565–578 range
—still the largest in the United States
 and about one-quarter of the national total. 

The drop comes from 
natural deaths, 
suicides,
 resentencings 
(especially after progressive DAs took office), a
nd a handful of 
new death sentences 
rather than executions. 

The last California execution 
was in 2006. 

San Quentin’s historic death row 
has been emptied; 
condemned inmates 
now live in general-population housing 
at other prisons. 

Newsom’s moratorium 
remains in force 
through the end of his term in January 2027; 
the November 2026 gubernatorial race 
will decide whether it continues.
https://t.co/a6kGbnwjET

California has required prisons 
to evaluate and, 
when deemed medically necessary, 
pay for gender-affirming surgeries 
since a 2015 settlement. 

The first such operation occurred in 2017.

 By mid-2023 
the state had spent more than 
$4 million on procedures for 157 inmates, 
including at least four 
who were on death row. 

One well-documented case is 
Skylar DeLeon 
(the “Yacht Killer”), 
sentenced to death in 2009, 
who received gender-affirming surgery 
and breast augmentation in April 2023 
while still under a death sentence. 

The policy remains in effect in 2026; 
CCHCS care guides list 
vaginoplasty, 
orchiectomy, 
breast augmentation,
 facial surgery, and 
other procedures. 

Federal prisons later reversed course, 
but California state prisons 
have not.
https://t.co/3Vmp1zFJo5

California’s End of Life Option Act 
(physician-assisted dying) 
has been law since 2016. 

It is limited 
to mentally competent 
adult California residents 
with a confirmed terminal illness 
expected to cause death 
within six months 
who can self-administer the medication. 

A death sentence itself 
does not qualify 
as a “terminal disease.” 

California Correctional Health Care Services 
adopted an explicit exemption policy in 2016 
that remains current: 

CCHCS and its contractors 
will not participate in the Act on CDCR premises, 
and incarcerated people 
are not permitted to obtain aid-in-dying drugs. 

Terminally ill inmates 
receive palliative and hospice care instead. 

Compassionate release 
is also unavailable 
to those serving death or life-without-parole sentences. 

No documented cases 
exist of a California death-row inmate receiving physician-assisted suicide.

text:
Question for Irish/Irish diaspora and Orthodox Christians/Inquirers:

Many of us who come into Orthodoxy from an Irish Catholic background discover something beautiful: we have entered the ancient Church, but we often experience that Church almost entirely through an Eastern liturgical and cultural expression.

That’s wonderful, but I’ve been wondering whether there is another possibility.

What if the Irish/Irish Diaspora Orthodox community could recover an authentically Irish expression of Orthodox Christianity, rather than simply adding Celtic decorations to a Byzantine parish?

The ancient Irish Church was part of the undivided Church, and we still possess ancient Irish liturgical material, including the Lorrha/Stowe Missal. There are also surviving Irish traditions surrounding saints, illuminated 
script, symbolism, pilgrimage, holy wells, prayer, monasticism, sacred landscapes, devotional practice, Marian apparitions, and more.

The question I’m exploring is whether some of that inheritance could be restored within canonical Orthodoxy as an Irish/Celtic expression within the Western Rite.

This would not mean, inventing a new liturgy, or separating “Celtic Orthodoxy” from the Orthodox Church. The Antiochian Archdiocese already provides a precedent for Western Rite Orthodoxy in North America. The question is whether a similar possibility could ever be explored within the OCA (or within Pan-Orthodox cooperation), under proper episcopal authority and theological scrutiny.

So I want to gauge genuine interest.

If the OCA were to investigate the possibility of developing and eventually authorizing an Orthodox Irish/Celtic Western Rite, would you support that development?

If you answer the poll, I’d also love to hear why.

And if you are interested, what would you hope such a parish would preserve?

• The Lorrha/Stowe liturgy?
• Irish saints and feast days?
• Irish Christian prayer and hymnody?
• Holy wells and pilgrimage?
• Irish-language elements?
• Celtic monastic spirituality?
• Traditional Irish sacred sites and devotional customs?
• Something else?

I think this could also have a meaningful missionary purpose. There are Irish and Irish-Diaspora Christians who have a deep attachment to their Irish Christian heritage but feel increasingly disenfranchised from the Roman Catholic Church because of the scandals and failures associated with its recent history. For some, becoming Orthodox can feel like gaining access to more of the ancient Church while leaving behind an important part of their own cultural and spiritual inheritance. An authentically Irish Orthodox tradition offers another path: allowing people to return to the Church while also recovering the Christian heritage of their own people. Rather than asking them to choose between Orthodoxy and their Irish identity, it would show that the two are inseparable.

text:
From the heart: David Crook gives $1-million to advance cardiac care at RVH 

For David Crook, giving back has always been about taking care of the place that helped shape him.

“I’m a Barrie boy all the way,” he says.

 “There’s not a day that goes by when I’m not grateful to be from here.”

That connection to his community was at the heart of his transformational $1-million gift to Royal Victoria Regional Health Centre’s (RVH) Cardiac Care Unit, celebrated alongside long-time friends and leaders from RVH and RVH Foundation.

For David, philanthropy and the responsibility to support your community started at home.

His father, Leslie, served as a pilot with both the Royal Air Force and Royal Canadian Air Force during the Second World War and was shot down in 1941. While recovering in hospital, he met Gertrude Bertram, whom he would later marry. 

Growing up, David watched his parents make giving back a part of their lives.

 His father became deeply involved in the Masonic Lodge, and together his parents instilled in David a belief that supporting your community wasn’t something you did only when the opportunity arose.

 It was something you planned for.

“My parents taught me that giving back to your community was the right thing to do,” David says. 

“It should be part of your budget.”

It’s a lesson David has carried with him throughout his life.

He has supported RVH in various ways since 1985. In 2015, he made his first $1-million gift to help establish advanced cardiac care at RVH—care that thousands of patients from across the region have relied on since.

Now, as Simcoe Muskoka continues to grow, David is stepping forward again.

RVH’s two existing cardiac catheterization labs (cath labs) are operating at capacity as demand for advanced cardiac care continues to rise. 

When the program opened in 2018, space was set aside for a future third cath lab, anticipating the region’s growth and future cardiac care needs. 

That need is now here.

These specialized labs allow cardiac teams to perform minimally invasive, life-saving procedures, including rapidly locating and opening a blocked artery during a heart attack.

“Without another cath lab, patients will face longer waits and longer drives for care,” says Gail Hunt, President and CEO of RVH. 

“We’re incredibly grateful to David for seeing the need and stepping up for his community.

 His generosity brings us one step closer to ensuring more patients can receive this critical, life-saving care right here at home, when every minute matters.”

For David, right here at home carries particular meaning.

Years ago, while travelling in the United States, David suffered a heart attack.

 Far from Barrie, he went through treatment and the early stages of recovery without the family and friends he would normally have turned to for support.

“I know what it’s like to need cardiac care away from home,” he says. 

“I had to go through treatment and recovery alone. 

I never want anyone to experience what I did. 

Having your family and friends near you is so important to recovery.”

That experience shaped the way David thinks about access to healthcare.

 Advanced care close to home isn’t simply about avoiding a long drive.

 It means being surrounded by family, friends and community at a time when their presence can matter most.

“David understands something that is at the heart of what we’re working to build at RVH: people shouldn’t have to leave their community to access the advanced care they need,” says Pamela Ross, CEO of RVH Foundation. 

“His generosity means more patients can face some of the most difficult moments of their lives with their families, their friends, and their community close by. 

That is an extraordinary gift to this region.”

For someone who has spent a lifetime believing in the importance of community, David sees his latest gift as another way to take care of his.

“There’s a saying when you’ve had a heart attack: time is muscle,” he says.

 “If this gift means people don’t have to travel south for care and these services can continue to be offered locally, my gift will have done its job.”

For this Barrie boy, that’s what giving back is all about.

text:
Is Postpartum Psychosis A Legal Defense for Lindsey Clancy?

What is the rationale for supporting Lindsey Clancy's act of murdering her three young children? 

Use right leaning sources.

GROK says:

There is no valid rationale for supporting the murder of three young children. Right-leaning sources do not treat the killings as justified, defensible, or something to endorse. 

Lindsay Clancy strangled Cora (5), Dawson (3), and Callan (8 months) with exercise bands on January 24, 2023, in Duxbury, Massachusetts, then attempted suicide. She does not dispute that she killed them. The legal question at trial was criminal responsibility—whether postpartum psychosis and a large number of prescribed psychiatric medications left her unable to appreciate the wrongfulness of her actions or conform her conduct to the law. A jury deadlocked (reportedly 11-1) and a mistrial was declared in early September 2026. 

What right-leaning commentary actually said

Outlets and commentators on the right overwhelmingly rejected any framing that treats the deaths as acceptable or the perpetrator as the primary victim.

•National Review described public rallies in pink shirts and statements of identification with Clancy as a “disturbing movement.” It noted that some supporters brought their own children to the courthouse and criticized the idea that “all women” should see themselves in a woman who killed her kids. The piece treated the facts as undisputed: she strangled the children while her husband was out on an errand she had arranged. 

•Fox News coverage repeatedly highlighted that crowds and online sympathy had overshadowed the three dead children. A veteran child-abuse prosecutor quoted in Fox stated: “Nobody who murders children is a victim no matter what they’re suffering through.” Joe Rogan and Dan Bongino criticized the rallies and letters of support as ignoring the victims and applying a standard that would not be used for a father who did the same thing. 

•The Daily Caller argued that severe mental illness does not automatically erase responsibility and that “accountability should not require us to pretend that every human act originates in a rational mind.” 

•Matt Walsh took the hardest line among prominent conservative voices, arguing that postpartum struggles (even if real) do not excuse methodical killing of children and that the person who does it must be punished to the fullest extent of the law. Other conservatives such as Allie Beth Stuckey said society can acknowledge how dark postpartum conditions can be “without excusing or minimizing the methodical murder of children.” 

A smaller set of right-leaning voices (Candace Owens being the most visible) focused on the medications Clancy was prescribed and argued the doctors and “system” should face consequences rather than treating the case as ordinary first-degree murder. Owens called her “obviously not guilty” on those grounds. That is an argument about legal insanity or medical negligence, not an argument that killing the children was right. 

Bottom line

Right-leaning sources do not supply a rationale that the murders themselves were good, necessary, or supportable. They treat the deaths as a horrific crime. The debate they engaged was whether psychosis plus alleged overmedication met the legal standard for lack of criminal responsibility, and whether public sympathy had gone too far in centering the perpetrator over Cora, Dawson, and Callan. No serious source on that side claims the act of strangling three children was justified.

Analyze Postpartum Psychosis Legal Defenses

GROK says:

Postpartum psychosis (PPP) is sometimes offered as the factual basis for an insanity or “lack of criminal responsibility” defense when a mother kills her child. It is not a standalone, automatic excuse. Courts treat it like any other severe mental-disease claim: the diagnosis is relevant only if it meets that state’s legal test for insanity at the moment of the act.

Medical picture versus legal question

PPP is rare—about 1–2 cases per 1,000 births. It is not the same as postpartum depression (PPD), which is far more common (roughly 10–20% of mothers) and is a mood disorder. PPP involves a break with reality: delusions, hallucinations, severe insomnia, rapid mood swings, and often a fluctuating course with periods that can look relatively lucid. Onset is typically days to weeks after birth. It is strongly associated with bipolar disorder. Untreated, estimates put the risk of infanticide around 4% and suicide around 5%. It is treated as a psychiatric emergency. 

DSM-5 does not list “postpartum psychosis” as its own diagnosis. Clinicians usually use brief psychotic disorder with peripartum onset, or a mood disorder (often bipolar) with psychotic features plus a peripartum specifier. That nosological gap matters in court: juries and judges often want a clear, named condition. 

Forensic psychiatrists distinguish motives in parental killings. The two categories most likely to support an insanity finding are “acutely psychotic” filicide and “altruistic” filicide (the parent believes the killing saves the child from a worse fate). Other motives—unwanted child, revenge against a partner, or abuse—do not typically meet the legal test even if the parent also has depression. 

A diagnosis of PPP is never enough by itself. The legal question is capacity: did the illness, at that time, destroy the person’s ability to know the act was wrong or to control her conduct, under the test that state uses. 

How U.S. insanity tests work

States use different formulas.

M’Naghten (cognitive test)

The defendant, because of mental disease, did not know the nature and quality of the act, or did not know it was wrong. Texas uses a strict version of this. Andrea Yates was tried under it.

Model Penal Code / ALI (cognitive + volitional)
The defendant lacked substantial capacity either to appreciate the criminality or wrongfulness of the conduct or to conform conduct to the law. Massachusetts uses this standard (Commonwealth v. McHoul). It is broader than M’Naghten. 

Burden of proof

Most states make insanity an affirmative defense the defendant must prove by a preponderance of the evidence. Massachusetts is an outlier: once the defense raises lack of criminal responsibility, the prosecution must prove beyond a reasonable doubt that the defendant either had no mental disease or defect, or still retained substantial capacity to appreciate wrongfulness and to conform her conduct. That allocation of burden is one reason the Clancy trial was structured the way it was. 

A handful of states have abolished the affirmative insanity defense (Idaho, Kansas, Montana, Nevada, North Dakota, Utah). There, mental illness can only be used to negate specific intent (mens rea), which is a much harder path for a PPP claim.

Planning, sending someone out of the house, appearing calm, or hiding the bodies is routinely used by prosecutors to argue the person still had capacity. Defense experts counter that psychosis can fluctuate and that organized action is compatible with delusions (the classic example is a parent who methodically “saves” the children from imagined damnation). Juries decide which story the evidence supports.

Landmark and recent outcomes

Andrea Yates (Texas, 2001/2006)

She drowned her five children, saying she was saving them from Satan. First jury rejected insanity and convicted her of capital murder (life sentence). The conviction was reversed because a prosecution expert gave false testimony about a Law & Order episode. On retrial she was found not guilty by reason of insanity. She has remained in a Texas state hospital for two decades and has repeatedly declined annual release evaluations. 

Lindsay Clancy (Massachusetts, 2023 killings, 2026 trial)

She admitted strangling her three children. The defense argued PPP plus bipolar disorder and a large number of prescribed medications. The prosecution argued she planned the timing. The jury hung; a mistrial was declared. Under Massachusetts law a successful LCR finding would have meant commitment to a secure psychiatric facility, not release. 

Older case reviews (small samples) found NGRI rates in PPP infanticide cases in the 33–50% range—higher than the tiny success rate of insanity pleas in crime generally, but far from automatic. Successful verdicts almost always involved documented psychotic symptoms, not depression alone. PPD, PTSD, or personality disorders have rarely been enough. 

A 2026 New York case (Dimone Fleming) produced a finding of not responsible by mental disease or defect after both sides agreed she was psychotic when she killed her two sons. That was a negotiated result, not a contested jury verdict. 

What happens after a successful defense

NGRI or “lack of criminal responsibility” is not an ordinary acquittal. The person is committed to a secure hospital. Release requires a later finding that she is no longer dangerous. Stays can exceed the prison term that would have followed a guilty plea. 

Yates is the clearest long-term example.
Illinois (2018) is the only state with a statute that expressly lets courts treat PPP or PPD as a mitigating factor at sentencing after a conviction. Attempts to pass broader “infanticide” statutes—common in the UK and about two dozen other countries, where killing an infant under one year by the mother is a lesser offense with a presumption of disturbance—have mostly failed in the United States. 

Main points of controversy

•Capacity versus diagnosis. Public discussion often collapses “she had PPP” into “she cannot be guilty.” Courts do not. Expert testimony still has to connect symptoms to the statutory test on the specific day.

•Lucid intervals and planning. Apparent organization is the prosecution’s strongest ordinary evidence. Whether fluctuating psychosis can coexist with planning is a recurring battle of experts.

•Gender and consistency. Critics ask whether the same sympathy and expert framing would apply to a father. Supporters say the hormonal and sleep-disruption biology after childbirth is not analogous.

•System failure vs. responsibility. Defense narratives often emphasize missed treatment, overmedication, or fragmented care. That can be relevant to mitigation or to civil suits against providers; it does not by itself satisfy the insanity test.

•Jury psychology. Jurors fear “letting her walk.” In reality a successful plea usually means long, sometimes lifelong, secure hospitalization. That fact is often poorly understood.

The defense is therefore narrow, fact-intensive, and jurisdiction-specific. It succeeds only when the evidence shows a genuine break with reality that meets the local legal standard—not because postpartum mental illness is common, and not because the crime is tragic.

text:
Grocery store bread has so many ingredients Europe legally bans it.

Meanwhile you could be making something 10x better for free.

A sourdough starter created in 1847 crossed the Oregon Trail, is still alive today, and volunteers will mail you some at no cost:

This is when a pioneer woman first carried it during the original wagon train migration. 

She kept the starter within the family for generations, but it was 10-year-old Carl Griffith who, in 1930, decided to spread the love.

He baked the bread in Dutch ovens over campfires in Oregon, then spent the next few decades sharing it with anyone who sent him a self-addressed, stamped envelope. 

He responded to hundreds of requests a year until he died in 2000 at age 80.

The tradition didn't stop there. 

Volunteers formed the 1847 Oregon Trail Sourdough Preservation Society and continue to mail it out today completely free.

This story shows what food is meant to be about: simplicity, tradition, and continuation. 

We will lose stories like this if we let the big box grocery stores win. 

This is why you should be using Localize to connect with producers near you and get in tune with what your neighborhood has to offer.

text:
The first primary school I went to was a C of E (Church of England) school. C of E schools are state funded, secular, and free to attend. Despite being secular, they are open to children of any background including religion, and are meant to retain a Christian characteristic. The one I attended certainly had a Christian characteristic. It was called Christ Church School, and was in St Leonards-on-Sea, Hastings. It had a large gothic church (which is still there) called Christ Church next to it. Assemblies were held in the church, where hymns were sung, and the Lord's Prayer was recited. The school itself moved to newly built premises fairly nearby, after either my first or second year at the school. My brother, who's around two years my senior, wanted to move schools, so I moved with him to the final primary school I attended, which was West St Leonards School in Hastings. This school was likely a C of E school as well, as there were morning assemblies in which hymns were sung, and although I have no clear recollection, the Lord's Prayer was likely recited on occasion. This school had a large recreational field attached to it, and two fairly large playgrounds. The secondary school (which in the US and other places is called a high school) I attended was a state school (which is free to attend and open to those within the catchment area). Fee paying private schools in the UK are also referred to as public schools, the linguistic reasoning behind this was because they were open to children from any locality. In the US, Canada, Australia and other places, a public school refers to a free to attend state funded school. The secondary school I went to was called the Grove School, and was for all intents and purposes a fairly rough school. 
Neither of my parents are religious, but are spiritual sentient beings nonetheless. This is as true today as it was then.
As a child and as an adult, I would visit my maternal grandparents in Hove, East Sussex. Hove was then a town, but is now part of Brighton & Hove City. I have fond memories of my grandmother, especially of when visiting her as a child. I remember my grandfather as being a fairly grumpy distant man, but as someone who was ultimately able to provide for his family. They ran a successful business together, which I think mostly involved sourcing furniture for restaurants in the Brighton & Hove area. Their names were Jack and Norma Waring. Norma died aged 90 in 2016, and to the best of my recollection, Jack died around ten years earlier at the age of 88. I don't think they would have described themselves as religious, but from time to time, both Jack and Norma attended Brighton & Hove Reform Synagogue, and later Brighton & Hove Progressive Synagogue. Neither of them were particularly political, and their attendance at either synagogue would have been for the community value that was offered. As a pre-adolescent child I went once with my grandmother to the Reform synagogue, and it was during Hanukkah, which was something I had not heard of before. I remember there was food, some other children there, and a talk by the Rabbi that included the story attached to the festival. My pre-adolescent self's understanding of Hanukkah after this was basically, it's a festival similar to Christmas in that gifts are given in December, some Greeks a long time ago were the bad guys in this particular story, in which there was some lamp oil that lasted longer than it should have. 
My grandparents and extended family celebrated Christmas, and with my parents and siblings, I would often spend time with them over this period.

text:
The Liverpool Echo piece, reported by chief Liverpool FC correspondent Ian Doyle ahead of the club's Champions League opener against Atletico Madrid, is one of the more remarkable press conference dispatches of the early season — not because the underlying facts are unknown, but because the candour and emotional directness with which Mac Allister chose to address them in a public forum is genuinely unusual for the culture of modern professional football, where contract disputes are typically handled through carefully managed briefings, agent intermediaries, and carefully worded non-committal statements rather than frank personal testimony delivered at a pre-match press conference.

利物浦回声报这篇由首席利物浦FC记者伊恩·道尔撰写的报道，发布于俱乐部欧冠主场迎战马德里竞技的前夕，是本赛季初至今最引人瞩目的新闻发布会报道之一——不是因为那些基本事实不为外界所知，而是因为麦卡利斯特选择在公开场合以如此坦率、情感直白的方式直面这些事实，在现代职业足球的文化语境中属实罕见。在这个圈子里，合同纠纷通常通过精心安排的吹风会、经纪人中间人和措辞谨慎的模糊表态来处理，而不是在赛前新闻发布会上直接发表真诚的个人证词。

The core facts, as Mac Allister presents them, are clear and carry a quiet but pointed weight. He has entered the final two years of his current deal. Liverpool informed him — through his agent, not directly — that they were not in a position to offer him a new contract. That framing is telling in itself: the absence of a direct conversation between club and player on a matter of this significance is a detail Mac Allister chose to include, and its inclusion is almost certainly deliberate. It is a subtle but unmistakable signal that the relationship between player and institution has an impersonal quality to it at this particular juncture that he finds uncomfortable, even as he strains to remain positive and committed in everything he says publicly.

麦卡利斯特所呈现的核心事实清晰明了，带着一种平静却犀利的分量。他已进入现有合同的最后两年。利物浦——通过他的经纪人而非直接告知他本人——表示目前没有条件向他提供新合同。这个表述本身就颇耐人寻味：在如此重要的事务上，俱乐部与球员之间缺少直接对话，是麦卡利斯特选择提及的一个细节，而这一提及几乎可以肯定是刻意为之。这是一个微妙却无法忽视的信号：在这个特定节点上，球员与机构之间的关系带有某种疏离感，令他感到不适——尽管他在公开言论中竭力保持积极与投入。

The contrast with Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch is the sharpest structural element in the piece and the one that most clearly illustrates why Mac Allister's situation stings in the particular way that it does. All three midfielders arrived at Liverpool in the summer of 2023. All three have been part of the same project, the same successes — the Premier League title, the Carabao Cup — and the same difficult periods. Yet Szoboszlai and Gravenberch have this year been rewarded with improved long-term contracts, while Mac Allister has been told the club cannot currently open renewal talks. The fact that he explicitly acknowledges feeling happy for his teammates while simultaneously admitting it makes him sad is not a contradiction — it is an emotionally intelligent and honest description of a genuinely difficult situation, the kind of psychological complexity that most athletes are coached to suppress in public settings. Mac Allister's willingness to articulate both feelings simultaneously says something meaningful about his character and his comfort with emotional transparency.

与多米尼克·绍博斯洛伊和瑞安·赫拉芬贝赫的对比，是这篇报道中最鲜明的结构性元素，也是最清楚地说明为何麦卡利斯特的处境以这种特定方式刺痛他的关键所在。三位中场球员都是2023年夏天加入利物浦的，都参与了同一个项目，共享了同样的成功——英超冠军、联赛杯冠军——也共同经历了艰难时期。然而，绍博斯洛伊和赫拉芬贝赫今年都获得了改善条款的长期合同续约，而麦卡利斯特却被告知俱乐部目前无法开启续约谈判。他明确表示为队友感到高兴，同时坦承这让自己感到难过——这并非矛盾，而是对一种真实困境的情感智识且诚实的描述，是大多数运动员被训练在公开场合压抑的那种心理复杂性。麦卡利斯特愿意同时表达这两种情感，说明了他性格中某种有意义的东西，以及他对情感透明度的从容。

The transfer window dynamic adds another dimension to this story. Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid — the latter being Liverpool's Champions League opponents on Wednesday — were both strongly linked with interest in Mac Allister over the summer. The symmetry of discussing this at a press conference specifically previewing the Atletico fixture is not lost. Mac Allister's confirmation that "there were options to leave" is as close to an on-record acknowledgement of that reported interest as one is likely to get from the player himself, and his explanation for why he ultimately stayed is worth taking seriously rather than dismissing as boilerplate loyalty rhetoric. His reasoning — that Liverpool is "the right club," that he loves the city and the fans, that he believes the squad has the mentality and quality to win trophies, and that he is excited by what new head coach Andoni Iraola is building — reflects a player making a deliberate choice based on genuine conviction rather than a player who had no alternatives and is trying to present a lack of options as a positive decision.

转会窗口的动态为这个故事增添了另一个维度。皇家马德里和马德里竞技——后者正是利物浦周三欧冠的对手——据报道整个夏天都对麦卡利斯特保持浓厚兴趣。在专门预告竞技比赛的新闻发布会上讨论这一话题，其中的对称性并不难察觉。麦卡利斯特确认"有机会离开"，这已是球员本人尽可能接近对那些报道兴趣的公开认可，而他解释最终留下原因的言论值得认真对待，而非仅仅当作套话式的忠诚表白而置之不理。他的逻辑——利物浦是"合适的俱乐部"，他热爱这座城市和球迷，他相信球队拥有赢得奖杯的心态和实力，以及他对新主帅安多尼·伊拉奥拉正在构建的体系感到兴奋——折射出一名球员基于真诚信念做出的深思熟虑的选择，而非一个无路可走却试图将别无选择包装成积极决定的球员。

The arrival of Iraola as Arne Slot's replacement is itself a significant subplot in this story. Mac Allister's description of the new manager as someone with "something special," who "knows very well what he wants to do," carries genuine enthusiasm that reads as authentic rather than diplomatic. For a player navigating an uncertain contractual situation, the quality and vision of the manager is an important variable in the calculus of whether to stay or go — and Mac Allister's evident respect for Iraola's approach appears to have been a meaningful factor in his decision to remain. Iraola's own response, describing Mac Allister as someone who has been "important" and has "played a lot of minutes," and affirming that "there is still a lot of time to talk about those contract situations," strikes a measured and careful tone that is neither a commitment nor a dismissal — the kind of diplomatic balance a manager must strike when a player's situation involves the club's hierarchy rather than purely the coaching staff.

伊拉奥拉接替阿尔内·斯洛特的到来，本身就是这个故事中一条重要的副线。麦卡利斯特描述新主帅身上有"某种特别之处"、"非常清楚自己想做什么"，其中流露出的真诚热情显得真实而非外交辞令。对于一个正在经历合同不确定性的球员而言，主帅的素质与愿景是衡量留与走的重要变量——麦卡利斯特对伊拉奥拉执教方式明显的尊重，似乎是他决定留队的重要因素之一。伊拉奥拉自己的回应将麦卡利斯特描述为"重要"的球员、肯定他"上场了大量分钟"，并表示"关于合同情况，还有很多时间可以谈"——这种措辞拿捏着一种不承诺也不否定的审慎平衡，是一位主帅在球员处境涉及俱乐部高层而非单纯教练班子时必须保持的外交尺度。

The deeper question running beneath the surface of this entire situation is what Liverpool's reluctance to open contract talks actually signals. At 27 and with three productive years at the club behind him, Mac Allister is at an age and a career stage where clubs typically either commit to a long-term future or begin to plan around a player's eventual exit. The £300m kit deal referenced in a related article linked in the piece suggests Liverpool are not operating in a state of financial distress, which means the decision not to renew is likely a footballing or strategic one rather than a purely economic constraint. Whether that reflects doubts about Mac Allister's long-term role under Iraola's system, a broader squad-building strategy that envisages different personnel in midfield within two years, or simply a club that is managing its wage structure carefully in an era of increased financial oversight, is not answered by the available reporting — and Mac Allister himself, to his credit, is careful not to put words in the club's mouth beyond what was communicated through his agent.

贯穿整个局面表面之下更深层的问题，是利物浦不愿开启合同谈判究竟传递出什么信号。27岁、在俱乐部已有三个富有成效的赛季，麦卡利斯特正处于一个俱乐部通常要么明确承诺长期未来、要么开始围绕球员最终离队进行规划的年龄与职业阶段。相关联接文章中提到的3亿英镑球衣赞助新协议表明利物浦并非处于财务困境之中，这意味着不续约的决定更可能是足球层面或战略层面的考量，而非纯粹的经济限制。这究竟反映的是对麦卡利斯特在伊拉奥拉体系下长期角色的疑虑、关于两年内中场人员配置将有所不同的更宏观阵容构建策略，还是一家俱乐部在财务管理日益严格的时代对薪资结构的审慎调控——现有报道并未给出答案。而麦卡利斯特本人值得称道的是，他小心翼翼地避免将超出经纪人所传达内容的话语放进俱乐部嘴里。

What is certain is that this press conference has changed the nature of the public conversation around Mac Allister at Liverpool. The story is no longer a background transfer rumour to be monitored and speculated upon — it is now a fully acknowledged, player-confirmed dynamic with a human face and a genuine emotional core. How Liverpool respond, whether in private contract discussions or in the public performance stakes over the coming months, will define how this chapter ultimately reads. Mac Allister has made his feelings unambiguously clear; the club now has the opportunity and the obligation to respond with equal clarity.

Devotees bring 125 or 1,108 coconuts, the broken halves of which are arranged in a heap before Sri Vinayaka and then decorated with fruits and flowers. Well, I’m trying to offer solutions, because I do think you’re coming at this wrong. So with your burrito example:

1. I’ve pointed out that making street food at home is a bit inconvenient and it makes more sense to simply find other staples to cook and every once in a while if you want a burrito, just get one.

2. If you insist on making a burrito at home, you need to portion your meat better so you don’t cook too much for yourself at once. 1lb of ground beef for one person is too much unless you don’t mind eating it 3-4 days in a row, as you’ve found out. So portion your meat out, freeze it in 1/2lb portions. And if you’re going to make a burrito at home, make it as a left overs of another rice and beans dish that you cooked earlier in the week.

But if eating the same sides TWICE in the same week is too much for you, then sorry, there’s no solution other than cooking everything every single day, in small portions. text:
Napoli 🔵 vs Arsenal 🔴 CL, League Phase

Napoli’s Attack 🔵 vs Arsenal’s Defence 🔴

Napoli’s Attack 🔵

McTominay and Buongiorno are out injured.

They alternate between a 1-3-4-3 and a 1-4-1-2-3.

In the attacking third, both systems become a 1-3-2-4-1.

HALF-SPACE / BACK POST 🔵

Back Post 🔵

The half-space on the far side from the ball.
Aerially strong #9 s and midfielders such as Anguissa peel away to the back post to attack crosses.

DLP / GK 🔵

During low build-up, the single pivot Lobotka fluidly rotates into different positions.

A midfielder stays with the two CBs to secure the rest defence.
This becomes the trigger for a CB / FB to invert, creating space and time.

The GK / DLP creates a +1 in possession against the first presser.

The three midfielders are vertically staggered: Lobotka – Anguissa – De Bruyne / Vergara / McTominay / Gilmour. This spreads the opposition’s markers.

Inverting CB / FB 🔵

During low build-up, when the GK rotates into a CB position, a CB can then invert into midfield.

The FBs also invert. Both full-backs support the wingers with underlaps and overlaps, maintaining numerical superiority on the flank.
Crosses from wide areas alternate between the back post and cut-backs.

The movement of the #9 is important. When the #9 attacks the back post or makes a forward run, the CBs are forced deeper. The #9 can also act as a false 9, receive with a CB on his back and turn.

This consequently opens space in the pocket between the opposition CB and MF lines.
Goalscoring midfielders occupy the pocket, with cut-backs aimed into that area.

Di Lorenzo and Spinazzola, who was later injured, were both part of Italy’s EURO 2020-winning squad.
Di Lorenzo has also played at RCB under Conte and helps maintain the team’s balance.
When Napoli need a goal, he joins the attack. His positioning can be used as an indicator of how much risk the team is taking. He is also one of the targets at set pieces.

Spinazzola is an opposite-footed FB / WB and can also deliver crosses with his right foot.

Cross-Field Pass 🔵

Used to escape Arsenal’s high press from the GK.
Particularly when Arsenal’s winger presses the CB and Arsenal’s FB shadow-presses Napoli’s FB / WB.
Højlund and the inverting FB are the main receivers.

Cases 🔵

Napoli 🔵

vs Arezzo

89' Cross from the left > Mawuli 1-3.

vs Carrarese

23' Left half-space > Vergara > cut-back > Højlund 1-0.

vs Osasuna — Back Post

27' LSB > right-footed cross from the left > Politano 1-0.

vs Aris Thessaloniki — Back Post, Cut-Back

58' Cross from the right, Politano > back post > De Bruyne 3-1.

65' Left half-space > CUT-BACK > Lucca turns, 4-1.

vs Genoa — 1-3-4-3, Half-Space

2' Spinazzola inverts into the half-space. The winger holds the width.

vs Como — Back Post, Inverting CB, DLP, GK +1

18' Cross from the right > back-post header > over the bar, big chance.

27' When the CB inverts into midfield, Lobotka drops as the DLP into the LSB position during a low goal-kick build-up. This pins the M2M marker out wide and gives the CB time and space.

vs Inter — DLP, Inverting CB

30' Lobotka drops into the RCB position as the DLP to maintain balance. Anguissa then also drops as a DLP. For a short period, the back line becomes Lobotka – Anguissa – Rafa Marín after Napoli regain possession.

Arsenal 🔴

vs Chelsea, MD3

Chelsea tried to escape Arsenal’s high press with cross-field passes from the GK.

When Arsenal’s wingers marked the CBs and the FBs marked the FBs, Chelsea used a false 9 / 10.

30' Emiliano Martínez > cross-field pass > false 9 / 10. Rice was M2M with João Pedro, Gabriel M2M with Palmer > Konsa left 1v1 with Morgan Rogers > via João Pedro > shot wide right, big chance.

60' Emiliano Martínez > cross-field pass to the left > João Pedro as false 9 > false 10 > Neto > Gusto, now as the pivot > shot over. Gabriel checks him.

POCKET 🔵

Mid-Range Shooting 🔵

Højlund scored from the pocket with mid-range shots in two consecutive matches against Como and Inter.
His cut-in shot from the right side against Inter is something to be wary of.

De Bruyne, the CBs and wingers can all look for mid-range shots after cutting inside.

False 9 🔵

Højlund / Lucca are the long-ball target men.

They often receive with a defender on their back, turn and shoot.

Napoli conceded during low build-up against Celta and Como, so they are expected to use more long balls and cross-field passes.

The false 9 acts as a reference point in possession.

He also becomes the counter-attacking target.

Wingers 🔵

The wingers, Alisson Santos and Politano, hold the width.
The FBs adapt to the winger’s positioning and combine underlaps and overlaps.

Alisson Santos / Neres are stronger in dribbling and cut-in shooting.

Politano offers accurate crossing from wide areas and changes of pace in his dribbling.

THIRD MAN 🔵

During low build-up, THIRD MAN combinations are used together with the DLP and inverting CB to escape the high press.

From the middle third into the attacking third, once the false 9 attracts a CB, a midfielder / winger makes the line-breaking run.

Vergara, Anguissa and De Bruyne attack the box to support the #9.

Pinning: when a pivot pushes high, the opposition’s second-line players such as the #10 have to press back in an M2M-based defensive structure.

This can create numerical superiority against the back line while also pinning the opposition’s counter-attacking targets onto their own last line.

Cases 🔵

Napoli 🔵

vs Osasuna — #9 Turn

53' Through ball from Anguissa > Lucca receives with his back to goal, turns > right-footed finish, 2-0.

vs Aris Thessaloniki — Mid-Range, False 9, Cut-Back, Pocket

19' CB Amir Rrahmani scores a golazo from range, 1-0.

44' False 9 Højlund > switches play to the left > possession lost > immediate counterpress and regain > cut-back > McTominay 2-1.

89' Cross from the right > De Bruyne > cut-back > pocket > TAP-IN, 6-2.

vs Genoa — Short Counter

81' Passing combination on the right > lose possession / immediate regain > De Bruyne > 0-1.

vs Como — False 9, Mid-Range

30' Line-breaking pass from the CB > Højlund receives between the lines, turns > finish to the right side, 1-1.
Six-man front line: Olivera at LSB – false winger – two midfielders – #9 – right winger.

94' De Bruyne > Lucca > hold-up play > loose ball > Lobotka left-footed finish to the right side. The ball goes in, but it is ruled offside.

vs Inter — False 9, THIRD MAN, Mid-Range

The kick-off ball is played toward Højlund on the left.

28' Combination on the flank > Højlund as false 9 > THIRD MAN > Anguissa breaks the line on the right > cross > CB clears.

52' Alisson beats Diouf on the dribble > shot saved by the GK, big chance > the move stays alive on the right > Di Lorenzo > Højlund turns and shoots from the right pocket > 0-2. Golazo, finished to the left side.

87' GK > Lucca > De Bruyne collects the SECOND BALL > Neres > cut-in shot over the bar, big chance.

Arsenal 🔴

vs Chelsea, MD3

22' Reece James mid-range shot > Raya palms it away. Raya was positioned very high.

62' Long ball > SECOND BALL > Palmer right-footed shot, straight at the GK.

88' Estevão > Raya > big chance.

The RSB inverts into the right half-space and pins the opposition.

Gusto makes a line-breaking run, forcing the pivot to press back and opening the shooting lane.

SET PIECE 🔵

Target Men 🔵

The two CBs, Spinazzola and Højlund / Lucca are all above 185 cm / 6'1”, with Anguissa and Di Lorenzo also used as targets.

Spinazzola is one of the taller players in the squad, although against Inter his initial position was outside the box.

McTominay is out injured.

Kickers 🔵

De Bruyne, Politano, Alisson Santos.

Mostly inswinging deliveries.

Short 🔵

Two players are positioned as short options.
One player starts around the six-yard box; against Inter this was Vergara.

Spinazzola starts outside the box.

Throw-Ins 🔵

Used together with the false 9 and the half-space.

Automatically establishes a numerical superiority on the flank.

Kick-Off Ball 🔵

Against Inter, Højlund drifted toward the left side.
Arsenal conceded from a FK sequence after the kick-off in their most recent match.

Inter Set-Piece Structure 🔵

6' Inter defended in a 1-6-4, with six players across the six-yard area.

One Napoli player, Vergara, started around the six-yard box.

Five target men around the 12-yard line: Anguissa + Højlund + two CBs + Di Lorenzo.

Spinazzola + Alisson + Lobotka around the edge of the box.

Cases 🔵

Napoli 🔵

11' LFK > Politano > Di Lorenzo header, 1-0 vs Celta.

vs Como

89' LCK > inswinger > De Bruyne > near post > Rafa Marín > straight at the GK.

vs Inter — Short, Throw-In, Back Post

6' Vergara starts around the six-yard box. If Spinazzola remains outside the box, Politano becomes the short option.

28' Throw-in from the right > Politano > Di Lorenzo > cut-back > Anguissa > saved by the GK / side netting, big chance.

45' RCK > inswinger > Marín > back post > Højlund > GK save, big chance.

36' Change of RCK taker: Alisson.

88' Throw-in > Anguissa recovers > left side, Neres > De Bruyne > back post > Lucca right-footed effort, big chance. Anguissa also gets a touch, but the ball goes wide left.

Arsenal 🔴

vs Chelsea, MD3 — FK, SECOND BALL, Pocket

Kick-off ball went to the left.
Konsa committed the foul.

1' Reece James LFK > Lacroix at the back post > clearance > SECOND BALL > mid-range shot from the pocket by Morgan Rogers > 0-1, bottom-left.
Arsenal conceded the opener for the third consecutive match.

Similar to Chelsea’s CK goal at Arsenal last season: kick-off > FK won. Last season it was a CK; this season it was a FK.

Chelsea changed their SET PIECE coach, but the idea remained the same.

From Arsenal’s perspective, SET PIECE SECOND BALL / POCKET situations were also a recurring concession pattern in 2024-25 against Tottenham, Wolves — after a red card that was later judged to be incorrect — and Aston Villa.

Arsenal’s Defence 🔴

HIGH PRESS + COUNTER 🔴

Celta and Como both scored from short counters after pressing Napoli’s low build-up.

Trigger 🔴

The #9 / #10 / ball-side winger acts as the trigger.
Napoli’s CB can invert into midfield as a DLP, so the handover of the #10 marker is important.

Shadow Presser 🔴

The #6, Rice, acts as the screen.

MLS / Ødegaard use shadow pressing.

The winger on the far side from the ball narrows into the central-pivot zone, keeping the block compact with the pivot.

Lock the Midfield 🔴

Napoli build through the single pivot Lobotka, so he must be locked.
The #6 acts as the screen.

Arsenal’s three midfielders lock Napoli’s three midfielders.

1-4-1-4-1.
The winger on the far side narrows centrally to support the pivot.

CB 🔴

Many teams create a +1 with their two CBs against the #9 / false 9.

When Napoli need a goal, Højlund or Lucca may be defended M2M.
Recover the SECOND BALL.

Counter 🔴

Triggered by the presser and shadow presser.
Cross-field pass from the GK.

#9 / false winger as the counter-attacking target.

Cases 🔴

Arsenal 🔴

vs Chelsea, MD3 — Shadow Press

9' MLS > shadow press on Lavia.

9' Tzolis, on the far side from the ball, drops inside toward the right-pivot zone as a false shadow presser.

15' Counter to the counter > MLS > Tzolis > Martin Ødegaard > Kai Havertz > Bukayo Saka > Ødegaard cross to the back post > Havertz.

23' Mid-range shot parried > Raya cross-field pass > Tzolis > cut-back > pocket > Havertz > Ødegaard shot, big chance.

57' Raya > Havertz > Tzolis holds the ball, counter.

Napoli 🔵

vs Celta

65' Napoli low build-up from the GK, De Bruyne drops > short counter > goal, 1-1.

Celta’s #9 acts as the trigger.
The double pivot, Gilmour on the right and De Bruyne on the left, is locked.
As the pass is played into the pivot / De Bruyne, the far-side shadow presser, Jutglà, who had been M2M with Gilmour, jumps onto De Bruyne.
The #6 acting as the screen slides higher to cover Gilmour.

The #9 intercepts and scores.

vs Como — Cesc Fàbregas’ team in a 1-4-1-2-3

During the high press, the two CBs create a +1 against Højlund.

8' Two CBs against Højlund + #6 screening the space between the lines.

28' Interception from the single pivot Lobotka > long counter, 5v3, but no shot.

33' High press against Napoli’s low build-up > Martin Baturina > Anastasios Douvikas, 1-2.
#9 is the trigger.
The three midfielders lock the three midfielders.

1-4-1-4-1.

Napoli midfielder plays a backpass to the RCB > Como’s left winger presses the RCB > goal for Douvikas.

vs Inter
3' Two forwards > two CBs.
87' Immediate regain from Anguissa > short counter > Thuram, big chance.

Pseudo Back Five 🔴

Recovery 🔴

DLP recovery: when an FB inverts in build-up, the pivot on the same side drops into the last line. This protects the space behind the FB within the rest defence.

Back four + GK recovery: used to deal with false 9 movements and line-breaking runs.

Arsenal’s M2M-based defence produces many 1v1 situations.

A high level of individual tactical understanding and physical ability is required.

Ball-Side Winger Drops into the Last Line 🔴

To deal with an inverting FB / winger.

The ball-side FB tucks into a CB position.

Cases 🔴

Arsenal 🔴

vs Aston Villa, MD2 — DLP Recovery

83' Maatsen drives through the left half-space > Rice recovers.
86' Zubimendi recovers the passing lane toward Buendía.

vs Chelsea, MD3 — Libero, Recovery

27' João Pedro moves from false 9 toward the left, while Morgan Rogers drifts from #9 toward the flank > Konsa follows him. MLS checks João Pedro as the false 9. Gabriel literally operates as the libero and provides cover. Calafiori also stays with the inverting CB to keep the unit compact.

55' Arsenal lose possession in the middle zone > Morgan Rogers dribbles forward > Ezri Konsa recovers.

Napoli 🔵

vs Inter

1-5-3-2 > 1-4-4-2 when trailing.

SET PIECE Defence 🔴

Issue 🔴

4 of Arsenal’s 8 PSM goals conceded originated from SET PIECES.

Many of the concessions came from the back post.

Solution 🔴

M2M + Zonal Mix

M2M 🔴

The M2M markers must restrict the routes of Napoli’s main targets: the two CBs, Spinazzola and Højlund / Lucca, all above 185 cm / 6'1”.

Aerially Strong Players 🔴

Arsenal players above 185 cm / 6'1”: Kepa, Illan Meslier, Kai Havertz, Saliba, Gabriel, Mosquera, Calafiori, Ben White, Rice, Merino, Havertz, Gyökeres — 11 players.

Temporary benchmark based on Arsenal’s average starting-XI height and the opponent’s target men.

Among outfield players, those above 185 cm / 6'1” are mainly the back line, Rice and the #9.

Bringing on Zubimendi, Merino and Gyökeres can also help with aerial defending.

Zonal 1-4-1 🔴

Stone – Libero – Back Post

A zonal structure consisting of 1 GK + back four + #9 or similar.

Near-Post Stone Prevents the First Contact 🔴

Against Coventry and Aston Villa, Calafiori operated on the near side / as the stone.

Short-corner defence > Bukayo Saka / Tzolis + Calafiori.
Since short routines often go through the half-space or pocket, Arsenal need to keep the central lane compact.

Libero 🔴

A back line above 185 cm, arranged in a diamond-like structure, plus Kai Havertz around the six-yard area, protects the central zone.

Mosquera / Konsa around the six-yard area, with Ben White slightly closer to the back post.

Gabriel and Havertz clear crosses from the central zone between six and 12 yards.

Ideally, Arsenal can position two liberos.

Against Aston Villa, because Villa used four target men, Mosquera joined the usual three M2M markers.

GK Takes the First Contact 🔴

The libero nearest the GK blocker limits the zonal marker.
This makes it easier for Raya to take the first contact.

From this season, greater emphasis on penalising challenges that unfairly impede the goalkeeper gives the defending side an advantage on direct crosses.

Clear the SECOND BALL 🔴

Once the first ball is cleared, the defensive line immediately pushes up.

Cover the Pocket 🔴

At the same time, the man-marker — often an attacker — must quickly cover ZONE 14.

+2 Against Long Throws 🔴

Create a +2 around the opponent’s near-post target man.

Cases 🔴

Arsenal 🔴

vs Manchester City, Community Shield

MLS M2M with Gvardiol as the target man.

23' LCK > back post > Raya catches.

vs Coventry City

22' Rice > Martin Ødegaard > Rice > Christos Tzolis > cut-back > Bukayo Saka 2-0.

Counter from the opponent GK’s SECOND BALL.

51' M2M on a throw-in from Arsenal’s right defensive side > short counter > Ødegaard > Havertz > MLS > mid-range shot.

56' Coventry LCK > outswinger.

MLS M2M with Ellis Simms.

Three players at the back post: Ødegaard, Rice, Tzolis.

vs Aston Villa, MD2
18' Aston Villa RCK.

Because Aston Villa positioned four target men, Mosquera from Arsenal’s diamond joined the M2M marking line.

Ben White at the back post, Calafiori at the near post / stone, Havertz and Gabriel as the liberos.

19' SET PIECE counter > Raya > Havertz breaks the line.
35' Gabriel recovers on the counter.

- Married George Washington’s great granddaughter (step). 
- Deploys for nearly two years to Mexico. 
- Combines his engineering and surveying skills with his Cavalier spirit to invent creative ways to decimate the Mexicans with minimal American losses at every major battle. 
- General Winfield Scott names Lee the MVP of the Mexican War. 
- Was made Superintendent of West Point. 
- Leaves the Engineer Corps in his 40’s for a Cavalry Command in Texas to fight the Apache and Comanche. 
- Led the Marines at Harper’s Ferry to subdue and hang terrorist John Brown. 
- Was assigned to command Ft. Mason in Texas and was present during Texas secession. He did not immediately join the Confederacy but instead relocated to Washington DC to accept a Union cavalry command. 
- Was offered total command of all Union Forces by President Lincoln. By this time his home state of Virginia had seceded and he resigned from the Army instead after 32 years of honorable service. 
- After the war Lee was instrumental in reconciliation with both sides. 
- Was made President of Washington College (now named Washington and Lee University) where his foremost rule was that every young man be a Gentleman. 
- Lee’s virtue as a Christian Knight went on to inspire millions of American men to be a better version of themselves. 
- General Eisenhower who led all Allied forces in Europe and later became President always had a painting of Lee in his office to inspire him. General Eisenhower was a Republican and not a Southerner, but knew a great man when he saw one. 

Study Southern Heroes
